first.subject: Synoptic table of amendments to the Brazil-Turkey-US draft resolution (L.76) asking the Commission to study the federal clause, the territories clause and self-determination for the Covenant.
first.evidence: Text is a comparative table of amendments to paragraph 2(c)-(e) of L.76: federal-state clause (Lebanon, Mexico, USSR), territorial application (colonial territories article), self-determination (Afghanistan/Saudi Arabia). Several subjects at once, in a resolution to the Commission; cited in SR.308, 309, 312 only as the table of amendments to para 2(c).

second.subject: Synoptic table of amendments to the joint Brazil/Turkey/US draft resolution A/C.3/L.76 (1950) on the draft Covenant, covering the federal clause, the territorial clause and self-determination.
second.evidence: The text is headed 'Analysis of amendments to joint draft resolution ... (A/C.3/L.76)' and sets out the amendments to paragraphs 2(c) to 3 (federal state, territories, self-determination). SR.308 and SR.312 describe it as the synoptic table. It concerns a General Assembly resolution and several subjects, not one article.

first.subject: Revised draft resolution (many sponsors) to prepare a declaration and an international convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination.
first.evidence: Rev.3 and Rev.6 text: decides to prepare a declaration and a convention on racial discrimination and asks the Commission to draft it. That is the racial-discrimination agenda item (later ICERD), not a Covenant article; debated in SR.1167, 1172, 1173.

second.subject: A draft resolution calling for a declaration and a convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination (1962).
second.evidence: Rev.3 and Rev.6 are titled 'Preparation of a declaration and an international convention on the elimination of racial discrimination'. SR.1167 and SR.1173 discuss it under that item, which is a different agenda item from the Covenants.

sonnet.note: Draft resolution on preparing a declaration and convention on racial discrimination.

opus.note: Draft resolution on preparing a declaration and convention on racial discrimination

first.subject: US-Yugoslav joint amendment to draft resolution L.76 on the Covenant: the drafting should take account of, and consistently apply, the principles and purposes of the UN Charter.
first.evidence: Text replaces preamble paragraphs of the draft resolution to the Commission with a general Charter-principles clause; A/1559 para 38 and SR.308 describe it as a joint amendment to L.76, voted with the preamble. General guidance for the Covenant, no single article.

second.subject: A joint US/Yugoslav amendment to draft resolution A/C.3/L.76 saying that the Covenant should be drafted in accordance with the principles and purposes of the Charter.
second.evidence: The text is a 'Joint amendment to the Joint draft resolution ... (A/C.3/L.76)' that inserts a 'Considers that in the drafting of the Covenant ...' clause. A/1559 para. 38 and SR.308 confirm it amends the resolution (SR.308 defers the vote to the preamble). It proposes no article.

sonnet.note: Joint amendment to a draft resolution on the drafting of the Covenant as a whole (Charter principles).

opus.note: Amendment to a GA draft resolution on drafting the Covenant generally

first.subject: Liberian revised amendment to L.1006/Rev.6 to extend the planned declaration/convention from racial to racial and religious discrimination.
first.evidence: Text replaces 'all forms of racial discrimination' by 'all forms of racial and religious discrimination' in op. paras 1(a)-(b) of the racial discrimination resolution; SR.1173 notes it was withdrawn. Concerns the separate declaration/convention item, not a Covenant article.

second.subject: A Liberian amendment to the racial discrimination draft resolution A/C.3/L.1006/Rev.6 that would add 'religious' discrimination.
second.evidence: The text amends operative paragraph 1(a) and (b) of A/C.3/L.1006/Rev.6 on the declaration and convention against racial discrimination. SR.1173 records that it was withdrawn. That is a different agenda item from the Covenants.

first.subject: Chairman's note on the Third Committee's order of work on the draft Covenants at the 17th session.
first.evidence: Text lists which articles are adopted and the order in which remaining parts (additional substantive articles, general provisions, implementation, final clauses) will be taken; A/5365 says the Committee accepted the Chairman's suggestion on arrangements. Pure procedure.

second.subject: The Chairman's preliminary observations (1962) on the order of work for the rest of the draft Covenants: additional substantive articles, then general provisions, then implementation and final clauses.
second.evidence: The text sets out the order in which the Committee will take up the remaining parts of both Covenants. SR.1172 says it was the Chairman's observations, issued as a document, and A/5365 says the Committee followed the Chairman's suggestion on arrangements (A/C.3/L.1017). This is procedure about the order of work.

first.subject: Lebanese procedural proposal that the General Assembly include in the agenda of its sixth session, as a separate item, the study of ways and means to ensure the right of nations to self-determination.
first.evidence: Text not in ODS (OCR says document not found); A/1559 para 47 (rejected 16-7-28) and SR.311 paras 19, 35, 44 call it a procedural proposal on the Afghan/Saudi amendment, i.e. agenda placement, not a proposed Covenant text.

second.subject: A Lebanese procedural proposal (1950) that the General Assembly put the right of nations to self-determination on the agenda of its sixth session as a separate item.
second.evidence: ODS has no text. A/1559 para. 47 records the rejected Lebanese proposal to include in the agenda of the sixth session, as a separate item, the study of ways to ensure the right of nations to self-determination (A/C.3/L.104). SR.311 calls it a 'procedural proposal'. It is about the agenda, not a Covenant article.

first.subject: Note by the Secretary-General reproducing the texts of the preambles and the articles of both draft Covenants adopted by the Third Committee at sessions 10-17.
first.evidence: Document text: 'Text of articles adopted by the Third Committee at the tenth to seventeenth sessions' covering the preambles and articles 1-16 (ICESCR draft) and 3, 5-26 (ICCPR draft); SR.1259 cites it for the final-form numbering of the articles in article 4, para. 2. Cited only in agenda headings and this reference; a compilation of many articles.

second.subject: Note by the Secretary-General compiling the texts of the preambles and articles adopted by the Third Committee at its 10th-17th sessions for both draft Covenants.
second.evidence: Text: 'Text of articles adopted by the Third Committee at the tenth to seventeenth sessions... Note by the Secretary-General', reproducing many articles; cited as background documentation in the agenda item 48 headings, not as a proposal on one article.

first.subject: Austria and Nigeria: amendment to article 2, para. 1 of the draft Declaration on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5459).
first.evidence: Text: 'amendment to the draft declaration (A/5459)', article 2 para. 1 reads 'No State, institution, group or individual shall make any discrimination ... on the grounds of race, colour or ethnic origin.' SR.1215/1217 (1963) discuss it in the debate on the draft Declaration; it is not an amendment to any Covenant or UDHR article.

second.subject: Austria and Nigeria amend article 2(1) of the draft Declaration on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5459) to forbid discrimination 'whatsoever' and to cover groups and institutions.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to the draft declaration (A/5459)'; the quoted paragraph concerns discrimination on grounds of race, colour or ethnic origin; the debates (A/C.3/SR.1215, 1217) are on the racial discrimination declaration, another agenda item.

first.subject: Recapitulation of amendments (Chile, Ethiopia and France, Israel, Uruguay, USSR) to operative para. 2(g) of the joint draft resolution on the first Covenant, concerning implementation machinery and petitions.
first.evidence: Text: 'Recapitulation of amendments to paragraphs 2(g), 2(bis) and 3 of the operative part of the joint draft resolution (A/C.3/L.76)'; SR.314 (15 Nov 1950): Chairman says the amendments to paragraph 2(g) 'were recapitulated in document A/C.3/L.109'. Procedural resolution on the Covenant as a whole and its implementation.

second.subject: Recapitulation of amendments to paragraphs 2(a), 2(g) etc. of the Brazil-Turkey-USA joint draft resolution (A/C.3/L.76) on the draft Covenant, mostly on implementation, petitions and a supervisory body.
second.evidence: Text: 'Recapitulation of amendments to paragraphs... of the operative part of the joint draft resolution'; A/C.3/SR.314 para. 9: amendments to paragraph 2(g) 'recapitulated in document A/C.3/L.109'.

sonnet.note: Recapitulation of amendments to a draft resolution on measures of implementation (Third Committee, 5th session); procedural, not a specific article.

opus.note: Recapitulation of amendments to a GA draft resolution (implementation, petitions, deletion of articles); procedural, not one article

first.subject: Saudi Arabia: amendments to preambular paragraphs 1 and 4 of the draft Declaration on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5459).
first.evidence: Text: 'amendments to the draft Declaration (A/5459)', paragraphs 1 and 4 of the Preamble; SR.1217 (1 Oct 1963) Baroody introduces them as 'amendments to the preamble of the draft Declaration'. Not a Covenant or UDHR article.

second.subject: Saudi Arabia amends preambular paragraphs 1 and 4 of the draft Declaration on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5459).
second.evidence: Text: 'amendments to the draft Declaration (A/5459)', preamble paragraphs 1 and 4; A/C.3/SR.1217 para. 45 (Baroody) introduces them as amendments to the preamble of the draft Declaration.

first.subject: Consolidated draft resolution of the Third Committee's officers on the draft Covenant on Human Rights (fifth session): priority for the Commission's work, improvement of the first 18 articles, the Charter's principles.
first.evidence: Text: consolidated draft resolution noting ECOSOC res. 303 (XI) and calling on the Commission to continue the draft Covenant; SR.318 (17 Nov 1950): Chairman puts 'a consolidated text of the draft resolution on the covenant on human rights' to the vote as a whole. Procedural, about the Covenant as a whole.

second.subject: Consolidated text, prepared by the Officers of the Third Committee, of the draft resolution on the draft International Covenant on Human Rights and measures of implementation (became GA resolution 421 (V)).
second.evidence: Text is a draft resolution with preambular and operative parts (commends the Commission, calls for revised draft, points on the first eighteen articles); A/C.3/SR.318 paras. 1 and 14: 'consolidated text of the draft resolution... put to the vote as a whole'.

sonnet.note: Consolidated draft resolution on the draft Covenant as a whole; no single article.

opus.note: Consolidated draft resolution of the Third Committee (1950) on the Covenant as a whole, covering priority, the first eighteen articles and implementation; not about one article.

first.subject: Chile and UAR sub-amendment to the UK amendment (L.1167) to article 2, para. 3(b) of the draft ICCPR, adding 'political' before 'judicial or administrative authority'.
first.evidence: Text: 'amendment to the amendment ... to Article 2 (A/C.3/L.1167) of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; A/5655 paras 8, 13 (tagged ICCPR 2) describe it as a sub-amendment to para. 3(b) of article 2. Draft article 2 of 1963 is final ICCPR art. 2 (remedies).

second.subject: Chile and the UAR sub-amend the UK amendment (A/C.3/L.1167) to article 2(3)(b) of the draft ICCPR by adding 'political' before 'judicial or administrative authority'.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to the amendment... to article 2 (A/C.3/L.1167) of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights... sub-paragraph (b) of paragraph 3'; report A/5655 paras. 8, 13-14, 26 on article 2; final ICCPR art. 2(3)(b) reads 'judicial, administrative or legislative authorities'.

sonnet.note: Sub-amendment to the UK amendment to para 3(b) of draft art. 2 (adds 'political' before 'judicial or administrative authority'): remedies.

opus.note: Chile/UAR sub-amendment to UK amendment (L.1167) on para 3(b) remedies of draft art. 2 CCPR: add 'political' before 'judicial or administrative authority'.

first.subject: Saudi Arabia's sub-amendment to the Chile/UAR sub-amendment to the UK amendment on draft article 2: replace 'political' by 'legislative' and place it after 'administrative', so the remedy is determined by 'judicial, administrative or legislative' authorities.
first.evidence: The text itself says 'article 2 of the Draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'. The report A/5655 (Third Committee, 18th session) discusses it under article 2, paragraph 3 (remedies), and both speeches tagged by the pipeline are ICCPR 2. Draft article 2 in 1963 is final article 2.

second.subject: Saudi Arabian sub-amendment to the Chile/UAR sub-amendment (L.1168) to the UK amendment (L.1167) to draft ICCPR article 2, para. 3(b): replace 'political' by 'legislative' so the authorities determining remedies read 'judicial, administrative or legislative'.
second.evidence: Text names article 2 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (remedies wording); report A/5655 paras 14, 27 discuss it under article 2 para. 3(b); in 1963 draft article 2 = final ICCPR 2; citing speeches tagged ICCPR 2.

sonnet.note: Sub-amendment replacing 'political' with 'legislative' in the para 3(b) remedies wording of art. 2.

opus.note: Saudi Arabia sub-amendment to L.1168 (remedies, para 3(b) of art. 2): 'judicial, administrative or legislative'.

first.subject: Poland's four amendments to the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (preamble, arts I, II, IV(b)).
first.evidence: The text names the Racial Discrimination Convention (A/5921, Annex), 1965. It is a different instrument from the ICCPR, ICESCR and UDHR. The citing speeches concern articles IV and V of that Convention, and none are tagged.

second.subject: Polish amendments to the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (preamble, arts I, II, IV(b) on prohibiting racist organizations).
second.evidence: Text heading: amendments to the draft Convention on Racial Discrimination (A/5921, Annex); cited in A/C.3/SR.1315 (1965) debate on CERD article IV; no citing speech tagged to a Covenant article.

first.subject: Brazil, Morocco, Sudan and Togo's amendment to the draft resolution on the economic and social consequences of disarmament (A/5923, para. 4): ECOSOC should bear in mind the needs of the less developed countries when studying how to use the resources released.
first.evidence: The text amends an ECOSOC-recommended resolution (A/5923). SR.1298 shows it was adopted as operative paragraph 4 of that resolution. It is a separate agenda item and concerns no Covenant article, and none of the citing speeches are tagged.

second.subject: Four-Power amendment adding an operative paragraph to the ECOSOC-recommended draft resolution (A/5923) asking ECOSOC to bear in mind developing countries' needs when transferring resources released by disarmament.
second.evidence: Text: amendment to draft resolution in para. 4 of A/5923; A/C.3/SR.1298 records it adopted as operative paragraph 4 of that resolution; not a Covenant article.

first.subject: Iran and Nigeria's draft resolution on 'Manifestations of racial prejudice and national and religious intolerance' (agenda item 61): the Secretary-General is to urge governments to submit information, and the item is to be kept on the agenda for the twenty-first session.
first.evidence: The text recalls resolution 1779 (XVII). SR.1298 discusses it under Agenda Item 61. It is a procedural draft resolution on another agenda item, and none of the citing speeches are tagged.

second.subject: Iran-Nigeria draft resolution on the agenda item 'Manifestations of racial prejudice and national and religious intolerance', asking governments for information and keeping the item on the agenda.
second.evidence: Text is a draft resolution recalling res. 1779 (XVII); A/C.3/SR.1298 lists it under agenda item 61; other agenda item.

sonnet.note: Draft resolution on racial prejudice and religious intolerance, a different agenda item (61).

opus.note: Draft resolution on agenda item 'Manifestations of racial prejudice and national and religious intolerance'; another agenda item.

first.subject: Czechoslovakia's amendments to the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (art. I para. 1, art. IV, art. VII).
first.evidence: The text names the Racial Discrimination Convention (A/5921, Annex), 1965. The citing records (SR.1315, L.1245) discuss articles IV and V of that Convention. It is a different instrument, so it has no final article in the ICCPR, ICESCR or UDHR.

second.subject: Czechoslovak amendments to the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (arts I, IV and VII).
second.evidence: Text heading: amendments to the draft CERD adopted by the Commission (A/5921, Annex); debated in A/C.3/SR.1315 (1965) and sub-amended by L.1245 referring to CERD article V; not a Covenant.

sonnet.note: Amendments to the draft Convention on racial discrimination, not the Covenants.

opus.note: Amendments to the draft racial discrimination convention (CERD), not the Covenants

first.subject: Philippines' proposed new articles on measures of implementation for the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: The OCR text is Chinese and garbled. L.1251, the financial-implications statement, and L.1268 and L.1274/Rev.1 cite it as the Philippine articles on implementation of the Racial Discrimination Convention. It is a different instrument, and none of the citing speeches are tagged.

second.subject: Philippines proposal of articles on measures of implementation to be added to the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: OCR text is the Chinese version only; citing documents A/C.3/L.1251, L.1268, L.1274/Rev.1 describe it as Philippine implementation articles for the draft CERD (1965); not a Covenant article.

first.subject: Jamaica proposes a new article for the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination: legislative steps to give effect to the right to freedom from racial discrimination and administrative and judicial responsibility for violations.
first.evidence: Text speaks of 'the right to freedom from racial discrimination'; SR.1316 says it is a new article to follow article VII of the racial discrimination convention (agenda item 58). Not a Covenant or UDHR article.

second.subject: Jamaica proposes a new article, to follow article VII of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, requiring States Parties to enact constitutional or legislative provisions against racial discrimination.
second.evidence: Text speaks of 'the right to freedom from racial discrimination'; SR.1316 treats it as a 'proposed new article to follow article VII' in the racial discrimination convention debate (agenda item 58), not the Covenants.

first.subject: Mauritania, Nigeria and Uganda propose amendments to articles I, II, IV, V and VI of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: Text header names the draft Convention on racial discrimination (A/5921 annex) and lists its articles I, II, IV, V, VI; SR.1315 debates it with the Czechoslovak amendments to that convention.

second.subject: Mauritania, Nigeria and Uganda amend articles I, II, IV, V and VI of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5921).
second.evidence: Heading of the document names the draft ICERD adopted by the Commission (A/5921); SR.1315 cites it on the 'resulting in acts of violence' wording of ICERD article IV.

first.subject: Sixteen Latin American Powers propose amendments to the preamble and many articles of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: Text: 'amendments to the provisions of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Racial Discrimination' (A/5921, Annex), covering preamble and articles I, II onward; cited in SR.1315-1316 as the 'sixteen-Power amendments'.

second.subject: Sixteen Latin American States amend the preamble and several articles of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: Heading: amendments to the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (A/5921); SR.1315-1316 discuss its ninth amendment on ICERD article IV.

first.subject: Draft final clauses (signature, ratification, accession, entry into force, territorial application) for the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: Text is final clauses; SR.1353 lists it under agenda item 58, Draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, 'Articles on measures of implementation'.

second.subject: Proposed final clauses (signature, accession, entry into force, territorial application) for the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: Text is final clauses of 'the present Convention'; SR.1353 lists it under agenda item 58, draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.

first.subject: Consolidated text of the substantive articles (I, II and following) of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination as revised by the Third Committee.
first.evidence: Text of articles I-II defines racial discrimination and States' obligations; SR.1344, 1346, 1350 cite L.1239, L.1241, L.1249, L.1262 as the adopted substantive articles of the racial discrimination convention.

second.subject: Text of the preamble and substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination as adopted by the Third Committee.
second.evidence: Text is ICERD articles I-II (definition of racial discrimination, special measures); SR.1344 chair: the Committee had adopted the preamble and substantive articles of the ICERD (A/C.3/L.1239, ...).

first.subject: United States sub-amendment to Poland's amendment (L.1210) to article IV(b) of the draft racial discrimination convention: adding 'with due regard for the right to freedom of expression and of association'.
first.evidence: Text amends Poland's amendment to article IV of the racial discrimination convention (prohibition of racist organizations and propaganda); SR.1315-1316 debate it in that context. Although it invokes freedom of expression and association, it amends the ICERD article, not a Covenant article.

second.subject: United States sub-amendment to Poland's amendment to article IV(b) of the draft racial discrimination convention, adding 'with due regard for the right to freedom of expression and of association'.
second.evidence: Text amends A/C.3/L.1210 on article IV (prohibition of racist organizations and propaganda) of the draft ICERD; SR.1315-1316 debate it there, and it was withdrawn in SR.1316.

first.subject: United States sub-amendment to Czechoslovakia's amendment to article IV of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, adding due regard for freedom of expression.
first.evidence: The text amends article IV of the racial discrimination convention (A/C.3/L.1220), not a Covenant article; SR.1315 cites it only in that debate. The freedom-of-expression wording does not make it an amendment to ICCPR 19 or 20.

second.subject: United States sub-amendment to Czechoslovakia's amendment to article IV of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, adding 'with due regard for the fundamental right of freedom of expression'.
second.evidence: The text names 'article IV' of the racial discrimination convention (dissemination of racist ideas, incitement); the citing speech (A/C.3/SR.1315, 1965) is in the CERD debate. It concerns another agenda item, not the Covenants.

first.subject: Committee resolution deciding that the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination will not refer to specific forms of racial discrimination.
first.evidence: The text names the racial discrimination convention only. SR.1315 and SR.1316 cite it as the resolution adopted at the 1312th meeting.

second.subject: Resolution deciding not to include in the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination any reference to specific forms of racial discrimination.
second.evidence: The text is a decision on the draft CERD. SR.1315 and SR.1316 cite it as the resolution adopted at the 1312th meeting. It concerns another agenda item.

first.subject: Nordic five-Power sub-amendment to Czechoslovakia's amendment to article IV of the draft racial discrimination convention, saving the civil rights set forth in its article V.
first.evidence: The text amends articles IV and V of the racial discrimination convention (A/C.3/L.1220 No. 2); the Covenants are not the instrument. The SR.1315 speeches are about incitement in that convention.

second.subject: Five Nordic states' sub-amendment to Czechoslovakia's amendment to article IV of the draft racial discrimination convention, safeguarding the civil rights set out in its article V.
second.evidence: The text names Article IV and Article V of the draft CERD. The job number 65-25658 shows it is from 1965, although the file dates it 1955. SR.1315 cites it in the CERD debate. It concerns another agenda item.

first.subject: Secretary-General's statement of financial implications of the Philippine proposals (A/C.3/L.1221) on implementation articles for the racial discrimination convention: a Good Offices and Conciliation Committee.
first.evidence: The text concerns implementation of the racial discrimination convention (A/C.3/L.1221 and the SR.1344 debate); it is a financial statement, not an amendment to a Covenant article.

second.subject: The Secretary-General's statement of the financial implications of the Philippine articles on measures of implementation for the draft racial discrimination convention (A/C.3/L.1221).
second.evidence: The text is a financial-implications statement about a Good Offices and Conciliation Committee under the draft CERD. SR.1344 cites it with the CERD implementation amendments. It is not about the Covenants.

first.subject: United Kingdom amendment to the Philippine implementation articles for the racial discrimination convention, deleting the word 'directly' in article 1, paragraph 5.
first.evidence: The text amends the Philippine implementation articles (A/C.3/L.1221) for the racial discrimination convention. SR.1344 lists it among the amendments to those proposals.

second.subject: United Kingdom amendment to the Philippine articles on measures of implementation for the draft racial discrimination convention: delete 'directly' in article 1, paragraph 5.
second.evidence: The text amends A/C.3/L.1221, the Philippine CERD implementation articles. SR.1344 lists it among the amendments to those articles. It concerns another agenda item.

sonnet.note: UK amendment to the Philippine proposals on measures of implementation (delete 'directly' in article 1, para 5); implementation procedure.

opus.note: UK amendment to the Philippine measures of implementation (A/C.3/L.1221), Third Committee, November 1965. This is the debate on implementation, probably of the racial discrimination convention, not a substantive Covenant article.

first.subject: Saudi Arabia proposes replacing article 40 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights with national committees receiving individual complaints, with appeal to the UN Committee.
first.evidence: The text names 'article 40 of the draft Covenant on Political and Civil Rights' (E/2573 numbering). The concordance (covenant_drafts_tc.csv, stage tc1966, ICCPR) maps draft 40 to final 41. It was submitted during the 1965 racial discrimination debate: SR.1344 says article XII of that convention was based on it. This is low-confidence, because the concordance maps draft 40 to the inter-State article while the Saudi text is about individual petitions.

second.subject: Saudi Arabian amendment to replace article 40 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights with a system of National Committees that hear individual complaints, with appeal to the UN Human Rights Committee.
second.evidence: The text says 'Replace article 40 by the following' (the E/2573 numbering). Concordance tc1966 maps E/2573 art. 40 to final ICCPR art. 41 (inter-state communications). The proposal's subject, though, is national committees and individual petitions, which art. 41 does not contain; individual petitions went to the Optional Protocol. SR.1344 cites it only as the model for CERD article XII (individual petitions). By its subject it matches no final article, so the answer is none. If you go by the number, it is ICCPR 41.

sonnet.note: Saudi Arabia amendment to draft article 40: national committees and petitions by individuals; implementation machinery with no matching final ICCPR article (closest are optional-protocol matters).

opus.note: Saudi amendment replacing draft ICCPR article 40 with national committees for individual complaints and appeal to the UN Committee. Individual petition went into the Optional Protocol, not a final Covenant article. The only citation is in the CERD debate.

first.subject: Latin American amendments to the Philippine implementation articles of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, adding a right of communications from individuals and NGOs to the Secretary-General.
first.evidence: Text is headed as amendments to the Philippine articles on measures of implementation (A/C.3/L.1221); SR.1344 shows it concerns the racial discrimination convention, not the ICCPR, ICESCR or UDHR.

second.subject: Latin American amendments to the Philippine implementation articles (A/C.3/L.1221) of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, adding communications from individuals and NGOs.
second.evidence: The text concerns 'communications concerning the application of this Convention' and amends A/C.3/L.1221. In A/C.3/SR.1344 it is introduced as an amendment to the implementation articles of the racial discrimination convention (agenda item 58, 1965). It is not about the Covenants.

first.subject: Netherlands amendment to the article on petitions (article 16 of the Philippine text) in the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: The document header names the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, agenda item 58. It is not about any article of the Covenants or the UDHR.

second.subject: Netherlands amendment replacing article 16 (individual petitions) of the Philippine implementation articles for the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: The heading reads 'Agenda item 58 DRAFT INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION ON THE ELIMINATION OF ALL FORMS OF RACIAL DISCRIMINATION'. A/C.3/SR.1344 discusses it as part of the petition screening under that convention.

first.subject: United States amendments to several Philippine implementation articles (role of the ICJ, the Commission on Human Rights and specialized agencies) for the racial discrimination convention.
first.evidence: Amendments to A/C.3/L.1221, the Philippine measures of implementation for the racial discrimination convention (SR.1344, SR.1346). It touches several articles and belongs to a different instrument.

second.subject: United States amendments to several of the Philippine implementation articles (A/C.3/L.1221) for the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, mostly giving the ICJ roles in place of the General Assembly.
second.evidence: The text amends A/C.3/L.1221 articles (1)-(17). It is cited in A/C.3/SR.1344 and SR.1346 (1965) in the racial discrimination convention implementation debate.

first.subject: Tunisian amendment to article 11 of the Philippine text: inter-State complaints, arbitration and referral to the ICJ, in the racial discrimination convention.
first.evidence: SR.1344 and SR.1353 place it among the amendments to the Philippine implementation articles of the racial discrimination convention. It concerns another instrument, not ICCPR article 41.

second.subject: Tunisian amendment to article 11 (inter-State complaints) of the Philippine implementation articles for the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: The text amends A/C.3/L.1221 article (11). A/C.3/SR.1353 (24 Nov 1965) says it became the basis of paragraph 1 of the inter-State procedure in the racial discrimination convention text. It is not about the Covenants.

first.subject: Ghana's (revised) amendments replacing the Philippine implementation articles with a reporting system and a committee of eighteen members, for the racial discrimination convention.
first.evidence: The text is headed as amendments to the Philippine implementation articles (A/C.3/L.1221). The debates (SR.1344, SR.1346) discuss it as an ICERD implementation proposal. The convention is not the ICCPR or ICESCR.

second.subject: Ghana's amendments (and Rev.1) replacing the Philippine implementation articles of the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination with a reporting system and a committee of States Parties.
second.evidence: The text replaces the articles of A/C.3/L.1221. A/C.3/SR.1344 and SR.1346 (Netherlands and others) name it as a proposal on the 'implementation provisions of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination'.

first.subject: Joint Ghana, Mauritania and Philippines text of the implementation articles (committee of experts, reports, complaints) to be added to the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
first.evidence: The title says articles are to be added to the racial discrimination convention adopted by the Commission on Human Rights. SR.1350 debates it article by article (article VIII, and so on). It is not part of the Covenants or the UDHR.

second.subject: Joint Ghana-Mauritania-Philippines text of the implementation articles (committee of 18 experts, reports) to be added to the draft Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
second.evidence: The title reads 'articles relating to measures of implementation to be added to the provisions of the draft International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination'. It was debated article by article in A/C.3/SR.1350 (1965).

first.subject: Netherlands amendments to Part IV of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights: amending draft article 32 (paragraph 1), replacing draft article 41 (exhaustion of domestic remedies), and inserting a new article after article 43 on individual petitions.
first.evidence: The text sets out three distinct proposals: (1) an insertion in article 32 para. 1, (2) a replacement of article 41, and (3) a new four-paragraph article after article 43 on individual petitions (which went to the Optional Protocol).

second.subject: Netherlands amendments to the draft ICCPR (A/6342, annex II, B, part IV) covering article 32, article 41, and a proposed new article after article 43 on individual petitions.
second.evidence: Amends multiple articles of Part IV (articles 32 and 41) and proposes a new article on individual communications.

first.subject: Secretary-General's statement of the financial implications of Italy's amendment proposing an ad hoc committee of eighteen experts, elected by ECOSOC, to assist on reports under the Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.
first.evidence: The document itself is a financial statement on the Italian amendment. A/6546 and the concordance (tc1966 row 'additional article after article 17, ad hoc committee of eighteen experts') list the proposal as 'not in the Covenant as adopted'. It is a proposed new article that was never adopted, so no final article.

second.subject: Secretary-General's statement of the financial implications of Italy's amendments setting up an ad hoc Committee of Experts for the ICESCR's implementation machinery.
second.evidence: The text is a financial-implications statement about a proposed committee of 18 experts and its secretariat costs, not an amendment to an article's substance. A/6546 para. 19 and SR.1401 cite it only for costs.

sonnet.note: Financial implications of an Italian ad hoc committee proposal; implementation and procedure, and the Covenant is not specified.

opus.note: Secretary-General's statement of financial implications of Italian amendments (ad hoc committee of experts); implementation machinery, not an article text

first.subject: Secretary-General's statement of the financial implications of the United States amendment (A/C.3/L.1360) proposing a Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights of ten experts elected by the States Parties.
first.evidence: The text describes the US proposal for a ten-member committee. The concordance (tc1966 row 'two additional articles before article 17') marks it 'not in the Covenant as adopted', and A/6546 para. 14 says the US withdrew the amendments at the 1401st meeting. The debates cite it together with L.1364 and it was tagged ICESCR 16 (the reporting article). It is a proposed new article that was never adopted.

second.subject: Secretary-General's statement of the financial implications of the United States amendments (A/C.3/L.1360) setting up a Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.
second.evidence: The text is a financial statement on a proposed 10-member committee and its secretariat. A/6546 para. 14 says it covered the US proposals, which were withdrawn at the 1401st meeting. The one tag (ICESCR 16) is for the speech, not the document.

first.subject: The Third Committee's adopted texts of the implementation and final clauses of the two Covenants: ICESCR articles 17-25 (part IV), articles 26 ff. (Add.2), the ICCPR article 39 bis on reports (Add.5) and article 41 on conciliation (Add.6).
first.evidence: The variants Add.2, Add.5 and Add.6 in the file each reproduce several articles, of both Covenants and of different parts. A single article cannot be assigned. The citing debates (SR.1435, SR.1437) are tagged ICCPR 45 and 43 only because they refer to the text of article 39 bis as adopted.

second.subject: Texts the Third Committee adopted: ICESCR Part IV (arts 17-25) and final clauses (Add.2), and ICCPR implementation articles 39 bis, 40 and 41 (Add.5, Add.6).
second.evidence: The variants give the adopted texts of many articles across both Covenants. Debates cite Add.5 for article 39 bis and Add.2 for the final clauses.

first.subject: Nine-Power amendment (India, Iran, Libya, Nigeria, Pakistan, Senegal, Sudan, UAR, Upper Volta) inserting a new article 39 bis on reports under the ICCPR (Rev.1, para. 1) and a further paragraph on conciliation (article 41 procedure).
first.evidence: The document's own text is not available: only the ODS error page of Rev.1/Corr.1 survives in the OCR. A/6546 para. 372 shows that Rev.1 para. 1 is article 39 bis on reports, which became ICCPR 40. Paras 380 and 400 cite the same document in the debate on the conciliation procedure of article 41, and the citing speeches are tagged 42 (35), 41 (26), 40 (5). It therefore touches more than one final article.

second.subject: Nine-Power amendment (India, Iran, Libya, Nigeria, Pakistan, Senegal, Sudan, UAR, Upper Volta) on the ICCPR implementation measures: new article 39 bis on reports, plus the inter-State complaint and conciliation provisions.
second.evidence: ODS text is missing. In A/6546, para. 372 gives Rev.1 para. 1 as new article 39 bis on reports (final ICCPR 40), and para. 400 cites it for the next articles. Citing tags spread across ICCPR 42 (35), 41 (26), 40 (5) and 28 (4), so it covers several articles.

first.subject: Text of the entire draft Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights and draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights as adopted by the Committee in its tenth to twenty-first sessions.
first.evidence: The title and content cover the full preamble and all articles of both Covenants. SR.1451 records the vote adopting the two drafts as separate wholes on this document.

second.subject: Full text of both draft Covenants as adopted by the Third Committee at its 10th to 21st sessions, put to the final vote.
second.evidence: The text opens with the ICESCR preamble and Part I and holds the whole text. SR.1451 and A/6546 para. 504 cite it only for the vote on each Covenant as a whole.

sonnet.note: Consolidated text of the whole draft Covenants.

opus.note: Complete text of both draft Covenants as adopted by the Third Committee; the Covenants as a whole

first.subject: The Committee officers' list of drafting and language corrections (terminology, French, Spanish and Russian texts) to the preamble and articles of both draft Covenants.
first.evidence: The text runs through the preamble, article 1, article 2 of the ICESCR and so on, with corrections in all languages. SR.1451 and A/6546 para. 504 describe it as 'minor drafting changes' to the texts in L.1414. It concerns no single article.

second.subject: Drafting and language corrections the Committee's officers proposed throughout both draft Covenants (preamble, art. 1, ICESCR arts 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and so on).
second.evidence: The text lists French, Spanish and Russian wording fixes, article by article, across both Covenants. SR.1451 and A/6546 describe them as minor drafting changes.

first.subject: Thirteen-Power draft resolution (Sixth Session, 1951) deciding to include in the Covenant on Human Rights an article: 'All peoples shall have the right to self-determination'.
first.evidence: The operative text itself proposes the new article, with the wording that became common Article 1 (identical in ICCPR and ICESCR; ICCPR 1 given as the instrument). The record A/2112 shows a vote on A/C.3/L.186 and Add.1 and Greek amendment A/C.3/L.205/Rev.1. The pipeline tag ICCPR+ICESCR 1 (one speech) agrees.

second.subject: Thirteen-Power draft resolution (6th session, 1951) by which the General Assembly decides to include in the Covenant an article reading 'All peoples shall have the right to self-determination'.
second.evidence: The operative text reads 'Decides to include the following article in the International Covenant on Human Rights: All peoples shall have the right to self-determination' (it became GA res. 545 (VI)). The article it asked for became common article 1 of both Covenants (ICESCR 1 as well). A/C.3/SR.643 (1955), tagged article 1, cites it in the debate on self-determination and permanent sovereignty. Formally it is a GA resolution, but its whole substance is the new self-determination article.

sonnet.note: Proposes an article on peoples' self-determination.

opus.note: Draft resolution to include in the Covenant the article 'All peoples shall have the right to self-determination'

first.subject: Israeli draft resolution on drafting and implementation of the Covenant: proposes classifying rights into two categories (immediately enforceable and progressively realized), in one covenant with two sections.
first.evidence: The text concerns the structure of the Covenant and its implementation as a whole, not one article. Speeches cite it as the 'Israeli suggestion for one covenant in two sections' (A/C.3/SR.388). A/2112 lists it among the procedural resolution's implementation documents. None of its 27 citing speeches carry an article tag.

second.subject: Israeli draft resolution on drafting and implementing the Covenant: sorts rights into immediately enforceable and progressive categories, with different implementation procedures for each.
second.evidence: The title is 'Drafting and implementation of the International Covenant on Human Rights'. A/2112 lists it among the documents on measures of implementation sent to ECOSOC, and SR.388 describes it as the Israeli suggestion for one covenant in two sections. It concerns the Covenants as a whole, not one article.

first.subject: United States amendments (and Rev.1) to draft resolution A of the Commission on Human Rights, on recommendations concerning international respect for the self-determination of peoples.
first.evidence: The document amends a General Assembly draft resolution on recommendations on self-determination (Seventh Session, 1952). It does not amend a Covenant article text. The debates (A/C.3/SR.447-450) treat it as amending draft resolution A, and no citing speech has an article tag.

second.subject: United States amendments to the Commission's draft resolution A (A/2165) on recommendations concerning international respect for the self-determination of peoples.
second.evidence: The heading reads 'Recommendations concerning international respect for the self-determination of peoples': amendments to the preamble and operative paragraphs of a GA resolution (later res. 637 (VII)), not to the Covenant text. The citing debates SR.447-450 (1952) are on that agenda item; none of them is tagged.

first.subject: Indian amendments (and Rev.1) to the United States amendments to draft resolution A on recommendations concerning international respect for self-determination.
first.evidence: It amends the operative paragraphs of the General Assembly draft resolution on self-determination recommendations (non-self-governing and trust territories, plebiscite). It is not an amendment to a Covenant article. The debates (A/C.3/SR.456) confirm this, and no citing speech has an article tag.

second.subject: Indian amendments to the US amendments (A/C.3/L.294) to draft resolution A on international respect for the self-determination of peoples.
second.evidence: The text replaces the operative paragraphs of draft resolution A (A/2165) on recommendations concerning self-determination, a separate GA resolution. It was debated in SR.456 (1952) under that item; no citing speech is tagged.

first.subject: Fifteen Latin-American Powers' amendments to the Indian amendments (L.297/Rev.1) to the United States amendments to draft resolution A on international respect for self-determination.
first.evidence: The document amends the text of the self-determination recommendations resolution (equality of rights, 'facilitate the exercise of this right', plebiscites) and not any Covenant article. See A/C.3/SR.458, where Mexico and Brazil describe it. No citing speech has an article tag.

second.subject: Fifteen Latin American Powers' amendments to the Indian amendments (A/C.3/L.297/Rev.1) to draft resolution A on self-determination, covering equal rights, 'facilitate the exercise' and plebiscites.
second.evidence: These are amendments to the operative paragraphs of draft resolution A (A/2165), the 1952 recommendations on self-determination, not the Covenant text. It was discussed in SR.458; no citing speech is tagged.

first.subject: USSR amendments (and Rev.1) to the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women: non-discrimination wording added to its Articles 1-3, and two new articles on implementing measures and territorial extension.
first.evidence: The text amends 'Article 1/2/3' of the separate Convention on Political Rights of Women, not the Covenants. The debates (A/C.3/SR.474, 475, 478) confirm this. The convention is another agenda item, so no final Covenant article applies.

second.subject: USSR amendments to the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women: non-discrimination clauses in articles 1-3 and new articles 4 and 5 on implementation measures and on territories.
second.evidence: The text reads 'amendments to the draft Convention on Political Rights of Women'. The citing debates SR.474-478 (December 1952) are on that convention, a different agenda item.

first.subject: USSR amendments to the formal clauses (reservations, disputes/ICJ) of the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women.
first.evidence: Text amends 'Article 7-A' (reservations) and 'Article 10' (disputes) of annex II to A/2156/Add.1; SR.474/478 introduce it as an amendment to the formal clauses of the draft convention on political rights of women. A separate convention, not the Covenants.

second.subject: USSR amendments to the formal clauses (reservations, article 7-A; settlement of disputes by arbitration, article 10) of the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women.
second.evidence: Text amends 'Annex II (Formal clauses)' of A/2156/Add.1; SR.474-478 (Dec 1952) cite it as the USSR amendment to the formal clauses of the draft convention on political rights of women, not the Covenants.

first.subject: Netherlands drafting amendments to the preamble and article 1 of the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women (direct or through freely chosen representatives; all publicly elected bodies).
first.evidence: Title and text refer to the draft convention on Political Rights of Women; SR.474 and SR.478 discuss it as an amendment to that convention's preamble and articles 1-2. Not an ICCPR/UDHR article draft.

second.subject: Netherlands drafting amendments to the preamble and article 1 of the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women.
second.evidence: Title: amendments 'to the draft convention on Political Rights of' women; SR.474 and SR.478 (Dec 1952) discuss it as the Netherlands amendment to that convention's preamble. Wording echoes UDHR art. 21, but the document concerns another instrument.

first.subject: Seven-power draft resolution opening for signature the Convention on the Political Rights of Women, with the convention text annexed (voting, eligibility, public office, formal clauses).
first.evidence: Text is a GA draft resolution with an annexed Convention on the Political Rights of Women; SR.478 debates it as the joint draft convention. A separate treaty on another agenda item.

second.subject: Seven-power draft resolution opening for signature the Convention on the Political Rights of Women, with the convention's text annexed.
second.evidence: Text: draft resolution 'Decides to open the attached Convention' and 'CONVENTION ON THE POLITICAL RIGHTS OF WOMEN'; SR.478 debates it as that joint draft resolution.

first.subject: Joint amendment adding an article to the Convention on the Political Rights of Women extending it equally to non-self-governing, trust and colonial territories (original article 8-A).
first.evidence: Text amends draft resolution L.330 (Political Rights of Women convention) by adding an article after article 7; SR.478 describes it as reinstating article 8-A of A/2156/Add.1. Territorial clause of another convention, not ICCPR art. 50.

second.subject: Joint amendment adding a colonial-application clause (original article 8-A) to the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women.
second.evidence: Text: amendment to the draft resolution A/C.3/L.330, adding a territorial-application article after article 7; SR.478 describes it as reproducing article 8-A of that convention's original draft.

first.subject: Indian amendment to the Convention on the Political Rights of Women: 'State' includes territories it is responsible for unless excluded on ratification (original article 8-B).
first.evidence: SR.478 (India) says L.333 restates article 8-B of the original draft, substituting for the joint amendment L.332 to the political rights of women convention. Not a Covenant article.

second.subject: Indian amendment adding a territorial-application clause (original article 8-B) to the draft Convention on the Political Rights of Women.
second.evidence: SR.478: India withdrew from L.332 and submitted L.333 'restating article 8-B of the original draft' of the convention on political rights of women; the text is a clause on States' territories.

first.subject: Five-power draft resolution asking ECOSOC to have the Commission on Human Rights give priority to the item on the right of peoples to self-determination at its next session.
first.evidence: Text only requests ECOSOC to ask the CHR to give due priority to the item (no article text); SR.524 records its withdrawal in favour of L.371; SR.513 lists it as a self-determination resolution. Procedural, so no article assigned.

second.subject: Latin-American draft resolution asking ECOSOC to have the Commission on Human Rights give due priority to recommendations on self-determination under GA resolution 637 C (VII).
second.evidence: Text is a GA draft resolution on the Commission's follow-up to resolutions 637 A-C (VII), not a text for a Covenant article; SR.513 and SR.524 list it among draft resolutions on self-determination, and SR.524 says it was withdrawn in favour of A/C.3/L.371.

first.subject: Joint proposal of twenty delegations (observations on the draft covenants) that the right of peoples and nations to self-determination be reaffirmed and kept in both covenants as their first article and in the relevant implementing articles.
first.evidence: Text is wholly about self-determination (GA res. 637(VII), 738(VIII), 'maintained in both draft covenants in the first article'). SR.582 and SR.637 present it as the self-determination proposal. The article is common to both covenants (ICCPR 1 = ICESCR 1); ICCPR chosen as the single instrument.

second.subject: Joint observations by Afghanistan, Burma, Egypt and other states on the draft covenants, proposing that the right of peoples and nations to self-determination be kept as the first article of both covenants and reaffirmed by all governments.
second.evidence: The text says the right of self-determination should be 'maintained in both draft covenants in the first article'. A/2808 para. 42 records it as observations on the draft covenants, and SR.582 says it is about self-determination. This is common article 1 (ICCPR 1 and ICESCR 1). It is a set of observations, not an amendment worded as treaty text, and it also touches implementation by administering powers.

sonnet.note: Observations/proposals of 20 delegations that the right of self-determination be kept in the first article of both covenants.

opus.note: Observations on the draft covenants (9th session) wholly about self-determination; proposes keeping the right as the first article of both covenants.

first.subject: Secretariat working-paper compilation of all amendments and proposed new articles to the draft covenants submitted by Governments and Third Committee delegations (per GA res. 833(IX)).
first.evidence: Text says it compiles amendments to all articles of the draft covenants. Citing tags are scattered (ICCPR+ICESCR 1, ICCPR 19, 20, 23; ICESCR 2), and the report A/3077 cites L.460 in connection with articles 1 and 2 among others, so no single article.

second.subject: The Secretary-General's working paper under resolution 833 (IX), compiling every amendment and new article governments proposed to the draft covenants.
second.evidence: Paras. 1-6 describe a compilation of all changes proposed to the texts of the articles. A/3077 cites it for articles 1 and 2, and the debates that cite it are tagged ICCPR 1, 19, 20 and 23. It covers many articles.

sonnet.note: Compilation of amendments and new articles across the whole draft Covenants; cited under several articles.

opus.note: Secretary-General's compilation of all amendments and new articles proposed by governments for both draft covenants; covers many articles

first.subject: Report of the Third Committee Working Party on article 1 (self-determination) of the draft Covenants, submitting a new text: 'All peoples have the right to self-determination'.
first.evidence: Text: Working Party appointed at the 655th meeting to consider Article 1 of the draft Covenants and adopted a text on self-determination. All eight tagged citing speeches are 'ICCPR+ICESCR 1'. Article 1 is common to both covenants; ICCPR chosen as the single instrument. Concordance tc1955 maps draft 1 to final 1 for both.

second.subject: The report of the Working Party on article 1, with its redrafted text on the right of peoples to self-determination ('All peoples have the right to self-determination...').
second.evidence: The text says the Working Party was set up to consider article 1 and adopted a text on self-determination. SR.670 and A/3077 debate it as 'the Working Party's draft of article 1', and all 8 tagged citing speeches are tagged ICCPR+ICESCR 1. This is common article 1.

sonnet.note: Report of the Working Party on article 1 (self-determination) of the draft Covenants.

opus.note: Report of the Working Party on article 1 (self-determination), with its proposed text.

first.subject: Note by the Chairman fixing the order of voting on the amendments to article 7 (just and favourable conditions of work) of the draft ICESCR.
first.evidence: Text is a procedural note on order of voting, but limited to draft article 7 of E/2573 Annex I. Concordance tc1956 maps draft 7 to final ICESCR 7. All citing speeches (SR.718, A/3525) are tagged ICESCR 7.

second.subject: The Chairman's note on the order of voting on article 7 of the draft ICESCR (conditions of work) and the amendments to it.
second.evidence: The title and text read 'order of voting on article 7 of the draft Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (E/2573)', and the paragraphs are on favourable conditions of work and remuneration. The concordance for tc1956 maps E/2573 draft 7 to final 7. A/3525 para. 51 and SR.718 cite it for the vote on article 7. It is procedural, but it concerns only this article.

sonnet.note: Chairman's note on the order of voting, procedural.

opus.note: Chairman's note on the order of voting on amendments to ICESCR art. 7; procedural, proposes no text.

first.subject: USSR amendment to add to paragraph 1 of draft article 10 that paid leave before and after childbirth be accorded to employed women at the expense of the State or the employer.
first.evidence: Text: 'In article 10, insert ... paid leave for the period before and after child birth'. A/3525 para. 90 and SR.730 describe it as the USSR amendment to article 10. 23 of 26 citing passages are tagged ICESCR 10; concordance tc1956 maps draft 10 to final 10.

second.subject: A USSR amendment adding to paragraph 1 of article 10 paid leave before and after childbirth for employed women, at the expense of the State or the employer.
second.evidence: The text reads 'In article 10, insert ... Paid leave for the period before and after child birth'. A/3525 paras. 90 and 112 cite it. The concordance maps E/2573 draft 10 to final 10 (protection of the family and mothers), and all 23 tagged citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 10.

sonnet.note: USSR amendment adding paid maternity leave to para 1 of draft art. 10 (protection of family, mothers).

opus.note: USSR amendment to draft art. 10 para 1: paid maternity leave before and after childbirth.

first.subject: Report of the Working Party on draft articles 11 and 12 of the ICESCR, submitting a combined text on the right to an adequate standard of living (food, clothing, housing) and continuous improvement of living conditions.
first.evidence: Text: Working Party adopted a combined text of Articles 11 and 12 beginning 'The States Parties recognize the right of everyone to an adequate standard of living, including food, clothing and housing'. The concordance (tc1956) maps both draft 11 and draft 12 to final ICESCR 11. Citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 11 (28 of 28).

second.subject: The report of the Working Party on draft articles 11 and 12 of the ICESCR, giving a combined text on the right to an adequate standard of living, including food, clothing and housing.
second.evidence: The text is the Working Party's combined text of articles 11 and 12 on an adequate standard of living. The concordance for tc1956 maps E/2573 draft 11 and 12 both to final 11. A/3525 paras. 133 and 143 and SR.742 cite it, and all 28 tagged citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 11.

sonnet.note: Working Party combined text of draft arts 11 and 12: adequate standard of living, food, clothing, housing; final ICESCR 11.

opus.note: Working Party report with a combined text of draft articles 11 and 12: adequate standard of living, including food, clothing and housing, and international co-operation. Final ICESCR 11.

first.subject: Afghanistan and the Philippines amend the draft health article: broaden the health definition to physical, mental, moral and social well-being, and reword the steps (child development and infant mortality; environmental and industrial hygiene).
first.evidence: Text amends the health article (right to the highest attainable standard of health; steps a-d) and asks it be renumbered 12. Concordance tc1956 E/2573 draft 13 = final 12. All 39 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 12; A/3525 paras. 146-150 discuss it with sub-amendments L.591 and L.593 on health.

second.subject: Afghanistan and the Philippines amend the draft article on the right to health (renumbering it article 12, deleting the WHO definition of health, adding reduction of infant mortality and environmental and industrial hygiene).
second.evidence: The text sets out the right to the highest attainable standard of physical and mental well-being, child development, hygiene, epidemic diseases and medical service, all of which is the substance of ICESCR 12; report A/3525 paras 146-150 treat it under the health article; all 39 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 12. The document's own number for the draft article is garbled in the OCR ('article 6s' and a proposed renumbering 'as article 12'), so the draft number given here is not certain.

sonnet.note: Afghanistan and Philippines amendment to the right to health article (highest attainable standard of health).

opus.note: Afghanistan/Philippines amendments to the health article (renumbered 12): infant mortality, environmental and industrial hygiene.

first.subject: Czechoslovakia proposes adding 'in the interest of the maintenance of peace and co-operation among nations' to paragraph 2 and a new paragraph on international scientific and cultural co-operation and contacts.
first.evidence: Title says article 15 but body says article 16 (science and culture, steps for conservation, development and diffusion of science and culture). Concordance tc1957 draft 16 = final 15. A/3764 paras. 68-81 discuss it under this article; all 33 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

second.subject: Czechoslovakia amends the draft article on cultural and scientific life: adding 'in the interest of the maintenance of peace and co-operation among nations' to para. 2, and a new paragraph on international scientific and cultural co-operation and contacts.
second.evidence: The text refers to article 16 of the draft Economic Covenant (the heading's '15' is an OCR slip) on the conservation, development and diffusion of science and culture. The added paragraph, as sub-amended by L.634/Rev.1 and adopted 47-9-16 (A/3764), became ICESCR 15(4). All 33 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

sonnet.note: Czechoslovak amendment to the science and culture article (draft art. 15/16): peace-oriented steps and international scientific and cultural co-operation.

opus.note: Czechoslovak amendments to draft art. 16 (science and culture): peace and co-operation; international scientific and cultural co-operation.

first.subject: Saudi Arabia's sub-amendment (with Rev.1) to Czechoslovakia's proposed paragraph on international scientific and cultural co-operation: States 'recognize the benefits' of such contacts rather than 'will encourage'.
first.evidence: Text amends the Czechoslovak addition (L.633) to the science and culture article. It was accepted by Czechoslovakia at the 798th meeting and adopted as the paragraph on international contacts (A/3764). Concordance tc1957 draft 16 = final 15; all 17 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

second.subject: Saudi Arabia's sub-amendment to the Czechoslovak new paragraph (L.633, para. 2): States Parties 'recognize the benefits to be derived from the encouragement and development of international contacts and co-operation in the scientific and cultural fields'.
second.evidence: Rev.1 wording is almost exactly that of ICESCR 15(4). A/3764 says Czechoslovakia accepted it and the paragraph was adopted as part of article 16. All 17 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

sonnet.note: Saudi Arabian sub-amendment (and Rev.1) to the Czechoslovak amendment on international scientific and cultural contacts.

opus.note: Saudi Arabian sub-amendment to Czechoslovak amendment L.633 on international scientific and cultural contacts (final 15(4)).

first.subject: Greece proposes adding at the end of paragraph 3 that States give particular encouragement to creative activity tending to the healthy development of the human personality.
first.evidence: Text amends paragraph 3 of the cultural article (freedom indispensable for scientific research and creative activity); title omits the number. Debated in A/3764 para. 72 and 79 and in A/C.3/SR.797-798 alongside the draft article 16 amendments. Concordance tc1957 draft 16 = final 15; all 18 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

second.subject: Greece proposes adding to para. 3 of the article on cultural rights an obligation to give particular encouragement to creative activity that tends to the healthy development of the human personality.
second.evidence: Para. 3 of draft article 16 concerns freedom for scientific research and creative activity (now ICESCR 15(3)). A/3764 paras 72 and 79 and A/C.3/SR.798 discuss it under article 16. All 18 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

sonnet.note: Greek amendment adding encouragement of creative activity to para 3 of the science and culture article.

opus.note: Greek amendment to para 3 of the cultural-life article: encouragement of creative activity.

first.subject: Costa Rica and Uruguay propose a new sub-paragraph (c) in paragraph 1: the right to benefit from protection of moral and material interests in scientific, literary or artistic production (UDHR 27(2)).
first.evidence: Text amends article 16 of the draft Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights. Adopted 39-9-24 in the Third Committee (A/3764) and became ICESCR 15(1)(c). Concordance tc1957 draft 16 = final 15; all 25 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

second.subject: Uruguay (with Costa Rica, Add.1) proposes a new sub-paragraph (c) in para. 1 of article 16 on the protection of authors' moral and material interests in their scientific, literary or artistic productions.
second.evidence: The text says 'amendment to article 16'. The Rev.1 wording is ICESCR 15(1)(c) verbatim, adopted 39-9-24 by roll call (A/3764). All 25 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 15.

sonnet.note: Costa Rica/Uruguay amendment (and Rev.1) adding protection of authors' moral and material interests to the science and culture article.

opus.note: Uruguay (Costa Rica) amendment adding sub-para (c) on protection of authors' moral and material interests (final 15(1)(c)).

first.subject: Belgium, Brazil, El Salvador, Mexico and Morocco propose the opening of the life article: right to life is inherent in the human person and, from the moment of conception, protected by law.
first.evidence: Text is the right to life paragraph 1; A/3764 para. 112 discusses this amendment on protection from conception, and the report lists it among the amendments to the right to life article. Concordance tc1957 ICCPR draft 6 = final 6; all 15 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 6.

second.subject: Belgium, Brazil, El Salvador, Mexico and Morocco propose that para. 1 of the right-to-life article read: 'The right to life is inherent in the human person. From the moment of conception, this right shall be protected by law.'
second.evidence: The text is the first paragraph of the right-to-life article. A/3764 para. 112 discusses its 'from the moment of conception' clause, and the report also lists it with L.644 and L.653 as proposing the inherent-right-to-life clause. All 15 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 6. The surviving OCR fragment does not name the draft article number.

sonnet.note: Right to life inherent, protected by law from conception.

opus.note: Five-Power amendment: right to life inherent in the human person, protected by law from the moment of conception.

first.subject: Israel proposes amended texts for paragraphs 2 and 3 of draft article 9 (prompt information of the reasons for arrest; prompt production before a judge).
first.evidence: Text is headed 'amendments to article 9 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'. Draft 9 is final 9 in 1958. All 19 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 9, and the A/4045 report rejects it under paragraph 3.

second.subject: Israel's amendments to paragraphs 2 and 3 of draft article 9 (being informed of the reasons for arrest; being brought promptly before a judge, with release on bail).
second.evidence: The text is headed 'amendments to article 9 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights' and covers arrest and pre-trial detention. At the 1958 13th session, draft article 9 was already ICCPR 9. The report A/4045 and SR.863 discuss it under article 9, and all 19 tagged citing speeches are tagged ICCPR 9.

sonnet.note: Israel, arrest information and prompt judicial review

opus.note: Israel amendments to paras 2-3 of article 9: being told the reasons for arrest, being brought promptly before a judge, bail.

first.subject: Greece, Saudi Arabia and Spain propose a sub-amendment replacing 'in accordance with the dignity of the human person' with 'with humanity and respect for their personal dignity' in the treatment of persons deprived of liberty.
first.evidence: A/4045 (ICCPR 10) describes L.700 as a sub-amendment to Tunisia's amendment L.692/Rev.1 to the paragraph on humane treatment. SR.882 (Rossides) says the sponsors withdrew it. The wording is that of final article 10(1).

second.subject: Sub-amendment by Greece, Saudi Arabia and Spain to Tunisia's revised amendment: persons deprived of liberty to be treated 'with humanity and respect for their personal dignity'.
second.evidence: The wording is about treating detainees with humanity and dignity, which is ICCPR 10(1). A/4045 names it as the sub-amendment to Tunisia's A/C.3/L.692/Rev.1 on that paragraph. SR.882 records Greece withdrawing it once Tunisia restored the word 'humanity'. The one tagged citation is ICCPR 10.

sonnet.note: Sub-amendment on treatment with humanity and respect for dignity

opus.note: Greece/Saudi Arabia/Spain sub-amendment to Tunisia's amendment (L.692/Rev.1): 'with humanity and respect for their personal dignity' for persons deprived of liberty; withdrawn.

first.subject: Seven-Power draft resolution on the Draft Convention on Freedom of Information, providing for discussion at the 14th session and inviting governments' comments.
first.evidence: The text takes note of the Secretary-General's report under resolution 1189 A (XII) on the Convention on Freedom of Information. It cites UDHR art. 19 only in a preamble. SR.899 and SR.902 debate it as a separate agenda item, with amendments in L.708. None of the citing speeches is article-tagged.

second.subject: Seven-Power draft resolution to discuss the text of the Draft Convention on Freedom of Information in detail at the fourteenth session and to invite governments' comments on it.
second.evidence: The text is about the separate Draft Convention on Freedom of Information, a different agenda item. It mentions UDHR article 19 only in the preamble. SR.899 and SR.902 debate it as the seven-Power resolution on that convention, and none of the citing speeches is tagged.

first.subject: Philippine and Syrian draft resolution to abolish the 'colonial clause' (territorial application of the Covenant), which concerns the Covenants as a whole.
first.evidence: The ODS text is missing, only the 'does not exist' page. A/1559 para. 18 says it was the Philippine/Syrian draft resolution on the Covenant's territorial application, adopted first on 1-2 Nov 1950. SR.302 (Mendez) says its aim was to end the colonial clause. It is a general resolution, not an amendment to one article. The 1955 A/2929 concordance ties it to ICESCR 24 only through a mixed reference list.

second.subject: Philippines and Syria draft resolution on the territorial application of the Covenant (removing the 'colonial clause'), adopted in 1950 as A/C.3/541.
second.evidence: The OCR text is only an ODS 'not found' page. A/1559 para. 18 and SR.302 describe it as the draft resolution on the territorial application of the Covenant. It is a policy resolution with no final article of its own, and no final Covenant article is a territorial clause. The single A/2929 citation tagged ICESCR 24 is a references table and does not show what the document is about.

sonnet.note: Philippines/Syria draft resolution on territorial application of the Covenant; text not available (ODS error page); not a specific article.

opus.note: Philippines-Syria draft resolution on the territorial application of the Covenant (1950). Procedural, and there is no matching final article. The OCR text is only an ODS 'not found' page.

first.subject: Joint draft resolution by Brazil, Turkey and the USA on the future work of the Commission on Human Rights. It asks for completion of the draft Covenant, study of the federal-state and territories articles, and further instruments on economic, social and cultural rights.
first.evidence: The text of L.76 is an omnibus resolution. A/1559 calls it one of two 'over-all' resolutions covering all the policy questions the Economic and Social Council put to the General Assembly. It covers several matters at once (federal state, territories, implementation, specialized agencies). None of the citing passages is article-tagged.

second.subject: Brazil, Turkey and US over-all joint draft resolution on the future work of the Commission on Human Rights on the draft Covenant (priority, the federal and territories articles, economic, social and cultural rights, implementation).
second.evidence: The text is headed 'Future work of Commission on Human Rights' and gives the Commission instructions on the Covenant as a whole. A/1559 calls it one of two 'over-all' resolutions, and none of its 76 citations is tagged.

first.subject: USSR draft resolution (Rev.1) recommending that the Covenant include many further provisions: participation in government, self-determination, and the rights to work, social security, leisure and education. It also asks for a State obligation to implement the rights.
first.evidence: The text of L.77/Rev.1 is an omnibus resolution on the principles for the Covenant. A/1559 calls it, with L.76, one of two 'over-all' resolutions. The A/2929 concordance tags it with ICCPR 21, 22, ICESCR 6 and 7, so it touches several articles equally.

second.subject: USSR over-all draft resolution asking ECOSOC to have the Commission include many provisions in the Covenant (participation in government, self-determination, work, social security, education, etc.).
second.evidence: The text is a GA draft resolution that criticises the first 18 draft articles and lists provisions to add across many rights. A/1559 treats it as the second 'over-all' resolution. Its A/2929 references are spread over ICCPR 21 and 22 and ICESCR 6 and 7, so it touches several articles, not one.

sonnet.note: USSR draft resolution proposing a range of rights (participation in government, self-determination, work, etc.) and general principles; several articles, not one.

opus.note: USSR draft GA resolution on the covenant as a whole, listing many missing rights (participation, self-determination, ESC rights)

first.subject: Saudi Arabian amendments to the revised Peruvian draft resolution on housing (Secretary-General to collect and disseminate information on housing needs).
first.evidence: Text amends operative paragraph 3 of a housing resolution (A/C.3/L.764/Rev.3); SR.940 cites it only as the chair's call to vote; no covenant article involved.

second.subject: Saudi Arabian amendments to operative paragraph 3 of the revised Peruvian draft resolution on housing (A/C.3/L.764/Rev.3), asking the Secretary-General to collect and disseminate information on housing needs.
second.evidence: The text amends a draft resolution on housing, a separate item of the agenda; A/C.3/SR.940 paras. 30 and 36 put it to the vote with the Peruvian housing resolution; no citing speech is tagged to a Covenant article.

first.subject: Israeli amendments (and Rev.1-3) to article 14 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights: tribunal, exclusion of public, minimum guarantees, appeal, compensation.
first.evidence: Text is headed 'amendment to article 14 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; all 30 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 14; A/4299 discusses it under article 14.

second.subject: Israel's amendments (and Rev.1-3) to article 14 of the draft ICCPR: competent tribunal, exclusion of press and public, minimum guarantees (trial without undue delay, in his presence, counsel), review by a higher tribunal, compensation for miscarriage of justice.
second.evidence: Title: 'amendment to article 14 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; all content is fair-trial guarantees; A/4299 paras. 33-37 treat it under article 14; all 30 tagged citing speeches ICCPR 14; TC 1959 concordance: draft 14 = final 14.

sonnet.note: Israel, amendments to draft article 14 (fair trial)

opus.note: Israel amendments and revisions to article 14 on fair trial: independent tribunal, exclusion of press and public, minimum guarantees, appeal, compensation.

first.subject: Italian and Japanese amendment adding a new paragraph to article 14: no one shall be tried twice for the same offence (ne bis in idem).
first.evidence: Text: 'At the end of article 14 add ... new paragraph 5'; A/4299 reports it under article 14 and it was replaced by L.821, which became art. 14(7); all 19 tagged citing passages are ICCPR 14.

second.subject: Italy and Japan propose adding to article 14 a new paragraph 5: 'No one shall be tried twice for the same offence' (ne bis in idem).
second.evidence: Text: 'At the end of article 14 add the following as a new paragraph 5'; A/4299 paras. 46-48: replaced by the seven-Power amendment A/C.3/L.821, which became article 14(7); all 19 tagged citing speeches ICCPR 14; draft 14 = final 14 (TC 1959).

sonnet.note: Italy/Japan, no one tried twice for the same offence (ne bis in idem)

opus.note: Italy/Japan: new para 'No one shall be tried twice for the same offence' (ne bis in idem, now art. 14(7)); replaced by L.821.

first.subject: Argentina, Belgium, Iran, Italy and the Philippines: replacement text for article 12 (liberty of movement, choice of residence, leaving and entering own country, restrictions).
