first.evidence: Rev.1 and Rev.2 are headed 'Article 12' / 'amendments to article 12 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; text is the freedom of movement provision; all 16 tagged citing passages are ICCPR 12.

second.subject: Five-Power amendment (Argentina, Belgium, Iran, Italy, Philippines), with Rev.1-2, replacing the text of article 12 on liberty of movement, freedom to leave any country and to enter one's own, and permissible restrictions.
second.evidence: Rev.2 title: 'revised amendments to article 12 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; content is liberty of movement (final art. 12, incl. the 'arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country' wording); A/4299 paras. 5 and 11; all 16 tagged citing speeches ICCPR 12; TC 1959 concordance draft 12 = final 12.

sonnet.note: Liberty of movement and choice of residence, leaving and entering a country.

opus.note: Five-Power amendment: liberty of movement, choice of residence, freedom to leave any country and enter one's own, restrictions clause.

first.subject: Italian amendment replacing paragraph 3 of article 14: juveniles charged with a criminal offence to be tried under special legal provisions promoting rehabilitation.
first.evidence: Text: 'amendment to paragraph 3 of article 14 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; A/4299 and SR.963 discuss it under article 14; 10 tagged citations all ICCPR 14.

second.subject: Italy's amendment (re-introducing Israel's withdrawn point d) replacing paragraph 3 of article 14: juveniles charged with a criminal offence to be tried under legal provisions promoting their treatment and rehabilitation.
second.evidence: Title: 'revised amendment to paragraph 3 of article 14 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'; A/4299 para. 41 and vote (k) under article 14 (rejected 33-12-26); A/C.3/SR.963 para. 11; all 10 tagged citing speeches ICCPR 14; draft 14 = final 14.

sonnet.note: Italian amendment on trial of juveniles, draft art. 14 paragraph 3 (fair trial).

opus.note: Italy: trial of juvenile offenders, rehabilitation; became art. 14(4)

first.subject: Chairman's note listing the amendments to article 14 in the order in which they were to be voted on.
first.evidence: Text lists Argentine, Israeli and Italian amendments to article 14 (L.805/Rev.3, L.795/Rev.3, L.820); A/4299 and SR.967 cite it as the voting order for article 14, all tagged ICCPR 14. Procedural in form but confined to article 14.

second.subject: The Chairman's note (Rev.3) setting out the order of voting on the amendments to article 14 of the draft ICCPR (Argentina, Israel, Italy, Afghanistan and others), paragraph by paragraph.
second.evidence: Text lists only amendments to article 14 (paragraph 1 tribunal/public hearing, paragraph 2 minimum guarantees) in voting order; A/4299 (voting on article 14 'in the order suggested by the Chairman (A/C.3/L.816/Rev.3)') and A/C.3/SR.967 para. 23 cite it for the vote on article 14; a procedural paper, but wholly about one article (final 14, draft 14 = final 14 in 1959).

sonnet.note: Chairman's working paper setting out the order of voting on article 14 amendments; procedural

opus.note: Chairman's suggested order of voting on the article 14 amendments (A/4299: 'Voting took place in the order suggested by the Chairman'). This is a procedural note, though its subject is ICCPR 14.

first.subject: Ceylon sub-amendment to Israel's proposed new paragraph on the right of a convicted person to have conviction and sentence reviewed by a higher tribunal, adding 'according to law'.
first.evidence: Text amends para (e) of Israel's revised amendments (A/C.3/L.795/Rev.2) to draft article 14. A/C.3/L.795/Rev.3 point (e) incorporates it, and A/4299 and SR.964 discuss it under article 14. All 3 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 14. The right of review became art. 14(5).

second.subject: Ceylon sub-amendment to Israel's proposed new paragraph on review of conviction and sentence by a higher tribunal 'according to law' (right of appeal).
second.evidence: Text amends paragraph (e) of Israel's A/C.3/L.795/Rev.2 on review by a higher tribunal; A/4299 and A/C.3/SR.964 discuss it under article 14; it became art. 14(5).

sonnet.note: Ceylon, review of conviction by a higher tribunal

opus.note: Ceylon sub-amendment to Israel's L.795/Rev.2(e): right to have conviction and sentence reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law (art. 14(5)).

first.subject: Mexico and Saudi Arabia draft resolution inviting ECOSOC to have the Commission on Human Rights study repeated trial and punishment for the same offence and report on a possible separate article.
first.evidence: Text refers the ne bis in idem question (L.803, L.817, L.821) to the CHR for study. SR.968 and A/4299 present it as a way of disposing of the seven-Power amendment (L.821) while the Committee voted on the other parts of article 14. All tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 14; the subject became art. 14(7). It is a referral resolution, so a strict reading of the rule for procedural motions would give none.

second.subject: Mexico/Saudi Arabia draft resolution asking ECOSOC to have the Commission on Human Rights study repeated trial and punishment for the same offence and report on a possible separate article.
second.evidence: Text is a draft resolution referring the ne bis in idem question (A/C.3/L.803, L.817, L.821) to the Commission; SR.968 treats it as a referral motion. Procedural, although the subject later became art. 14(7).

sonnet.note: Draft resolution asking the Commission to study ne bis in idem and a possible separate article; a procedural referral, not a text for a specific article.

opus.note: Mexico-Saudi Arabia draft resolution asking for a study of repeated trial and punishment for the same offence (ne bis in idem), made during the Article 14 debate. The subject became ICCPR 14(7).

first.subject: Afghanistan and Saudi Arabia revised amendment to the joint draft resolution: the CHR is to study ways and means to ensure the right of nations to self-determination and to prepare recommendations for the sixth session.
first.evidence: Text (L.88/Rev.1) is about self-determination. A/1559 para 46 says the Committee discussed it at the 309th-311th meetings as the amendment on the right of peoples to self-determination, and SR.310 is tagged ICCPR+ICESCR 1. It is an amendment to a resolution, not to an article, and it started the process that led to art. 1 common to both Covenants. ICESCR 1 is equally correct. The pipeline tag is 'ICCPR+ICESCR 1', a single tagged speech.

second.subject: Afghanistan/Saudi Arabia amendment to the joint draft resolution (1950) asking the Commission to study ways and means of ensuring the right of nations to self-determination.
second.evidence: Rev.1 text inserts a para. (d) into a joint draft resolution; A/1559 para. 46 describes it as a request to ECOSOC/CHR for a study, not a Covenant text. It is a precursor of common art. 1 but proposes no article.

first.subject: India's amendment replacing paragraphs 2 and 3 of draft article 19 on freedom of expression (freedom to 'gather' information; list of permissible restrictions).
first.evidence: The text is headed 'amendment to article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights'. A/5000 reports it under article 19, paras 2 and 3. All 6 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 19.

second.subject: India's amendment replacing paragraphs 2 and 3 of the article on freedom of expression (freedom to 'gather' information; list of permitted restrictions).
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 19'; A/5000 paras. 9, 12, 22 discuss it under article 19; all 6 tagged citations ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: India amendment on freedom of expression.

opus.note: India amendment replacing paras 2-3 of draft art. 19: freedom of expression and its restrictions

first.subject: Brazil's amendments to article 19 (anonymity not permitted; war propaganda and racial, religious or class prejudice added as grounds of restriction) and a conditional proposal to delete draft article 26 as redundant.
first.evidence: Text in part I amends article 19, paras 1 and 3, and part II is only a consequential, conditional deletion of article 26. A/5000 discusses it under article 19 (paras 1 and 3), and all 7 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 19. The main subject is art. 19.

second.subject: Brazil's amendments to the freedom of expression article (no anonymity; restrictions for war propaganda and racial, religious or class prejudice), with a contingent deletion of draft article 26.
second.evidence: Text amends article 19 paras. 1 and 3; the article 26 (final art. 20) part is only a consequential deletion if the art. 19 amendment passed. A/5000 treats it under article 19; all 7 tagged citations ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: Brazilian amendments to draft art. 19 (opinion and expression) chiefly; also proposes deleting draft art. 26 (final 20) conditionally, but main subject is art. 19.

opus.note: Brazil amendments to art. 19 paras 1 and 3. It also proposes deleting art. 26 as a result, but art. 19 is the main subject

first.subject: USSR amendment adding to article 19, para 3 a restriction ground for preventing war propaganda, incitement to enmity among nations, racial discrimination and slanderous rumours.
first.evidence: Text is headed 'amendment to article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights' and modifies its paragraph 3. A/5000 reports it under article 19 and its vote. All 6 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 19.

second.subject: USSR amendment adding to paragraph 3 of the freedom of expression article a restriction for preventing war propaganda, incitement to enmity, racial discrimination and slanderous rumours.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 19', paragraph 3; A/5000 para. 16 and the vote record put it under article 19; all 6 tagged citations ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: USSR amendment to draft art. 19 para 3: adds war propaganda, incitement to enmity, racial discrimination and slanderous rumours as grounds for restricting expression; cited under ICCPR 19.

opus.note: USSR amendment to para 3 (permissible restrictions) of the expression article, adding war propaganda, incitement, racial discrimination; debate tagged ICCPR 19

first.subject: Indonesian amendment (with Rev.1 and Rev.2, the last co-sponsored with India) adding to the restrictions paragraph of the freedom of expression article a ground for securing peaceful and friendly relations among nations and races.
first.evidence: Text titled amendment to article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, paragraph 3 (restrictions); A/5000 (1961) lists it among the article 19 amendments; all nine tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 19.

second.subject: Indonesia (later with India): add to paragraph 3 of the freedom-of-expression article a restriction ground for peaceful coexistence / promotion of peace and friendly relations among peoples and nations.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights', paragraph 3 (E/2573 draft, 1961 numbering matches final 19); A/5000 para. 17 describes it under article 19; all 9 tagged citing speeches ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: Indonesia, restriction ground added to draft article 19 paragraph 3

opus.note: Indonesia (Rev.2 with India) addition to para 3 of article 19 on restrictions: peaceful and neighbourly relations among nations.

first.subject: United Kingdom amendment to article 19: replace 'any other media of his choice' by 'any lawfully operated devices' in paragraph 2, and add protection of official information from unauthorized disclosure as a restriction ground in paragraph 3.
first.evidence: Text headed Article 19, paras 2 and 3, of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights; A/5000 and SR.1074/1076 (Oct 1961) discuss it within the article 19 debate; citing speeches tagged ICCPR 19.

second.subject: United Kingdom: in the freedom-of-expression article, replace 'any other media of his choice' with 'lawfully operated devices' (para. 2) and add protection of official information as a restriction ground (para. 3).
second.evidence: Text headed 'Article 19' quoting the wording of the expression article; A/5000 para. 10 and A/C.3/SR.1074/1076 discuss it under article 19; tagged citations ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: UK amendment to article 19 paragraphs 2 and 3 (media, protection of official information); freedom of opinion and expression.

opus.note: UK amendment to art. 19, paras 2 and 3 (media, protection of official information), as the text and A/5000 show.

first.subject: United States amendment replacing paragraph 3 of article 19 (restrictions on freedom of expression), adding a non-discrimination clause and a ban on prior censorship.
first.evidence: Text is titled amendment to Article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, paragraph 3; A/5000 lists it among the article 19 amendments; the citing speech is tagged ICCPR 19.

second.subject: United States: replace paragraph 3 of the freedom-of-expression article with a restrictions clause barring prior censorship and protecting the right to criticize the government.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to Article 19 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, paragraph 3'; A/5000 para. 15 and para. 31 (prior censorship) under article 19; tagged citation ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: United States, restrictions clause of article 19 paragraph 3

opus.note: United States replacement of article 19 para 3 (restrictions on expression; no prior censorship).

first.subject: Amendment by eleven Latin American States to article 19, paragraph 3: replace the 'special duties and responsibilities' clause by a ban on prior censorship with only subsequent liability as provided by law.
first.evidence: Text rewrites the paragraph on the exercise of the rights of the foregoing paragraph (freedom of expression); A/5000 para 14 and SR.1074 discuss it under article 19; withdrawn at SR.1077; citing speeches tagged ICCPR 19.

second.subject: Eleven Latin American states: amend paragraph 3 of the freedom-of-expression article so the rights are not subject to prior censorship but only to subsequent liability provided by law.
second.evidence: Text rewrites the 'special duties and responsibilities' restrictions paragraph of the expression article; A/5000 paras. 14 and 433 and A/C.3/SR.1074 (Nicaragua) treat it as an amendment to article 19 paragraph 3; all 3 tagged citations ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: Amendment to paragraph 3 on restrictions on expression (no prior censorship).

opus.note: Latin American amendment to para. 3 of the freedom of expression article: no prior censorship, only subsequent liability.

first.subject: Uruguayan addition to the joint draft resolution (A/C.3/L.76) of 1950 proposing a study of a permanent UN office (Attorney General or High Commissioner) to receive and investigate reports of violations as a measure of implementing the Covenant.
first.evidence: Text amends sub-section 2(g) of a draft resolution to ECOSOC/Commission on Human Rights on implementation measures; SR.314 (15 Nov 1950) and A/1559 treat it as an implementation proposal; no article of the Covenant is tagged or concerned.

second.subject: Uruguay: addition to the Brazil-Turkey-US joint draft resolution (A/C.3/L.76) asking the Commission to study a UN Attorney General / High Commissioner to receive and investigate complaints as a measure of implementation of the Covenant.
second.evidence: Text amends sub-paragraph 2(g) of the joint draft resolution on implementation machinery; A/C.3/SR.314 and A/1559 discuss it among petitions/implementation proposals; no article tag.

first.subject: Secretariat analysis (1950) of amendments to paragraph 2 of the joint draft resolution A/C.3/L.76 on the Commission's work on the Covenant, reproducing amendments (e.g. Yugoslav, USSR) proposing several rights be added to the Covenant.
first.evidence: Text is a compilation of amendments to a draft resolution; SR.304 (6 Nov 1950) cites it as the working paper on paragraphs 2(a) and 2(b) of the resolution; it touches several rights (suffrage, political participation, minority language) and no single article.

second.subject: Secretariat analysis (comparative table) of the amendments to paragraph 2 of the joint draft resolution A/C.3/L.76 on the draft Covenant (priority of work, additional rights such as political participation and minorities).
second.evidence: Text is a tabulation of amendments to paragraphs 2(a) and 2(b) of the joint draft resolution; A/C.3/SR.304 para. 2 describes it so; it covers several subjects, not one article.

first.subject: Ten-Power draft resolution on balanced and co-ordinated economic and social development, endorsing ECOSOC's continued study and asking UN organs to pay attention to it.
first.evidence: Text is a General Assembly resolution on an agenda item about economic and social development, not a Covenant article; the two citing speeches (A/C.3/SR.1119, SR.1124) discuss it as a separate agenda item and no article tags exist.

second.subject: Ten-Power revised draft resolution on balanced and co-ordinated economic and social development (Third Committee, 16th session, 1961).
second.evidence: Text is a GA draft resolution on economic and social development recalling resolutions 1392 (XIV), 1161 (XII), 1258 (XIII); citing speeches (SR.1119, SR.1124) treat it under that agenda item, not the Covenants.

first.subject: USSR amendments to the joint Brazil/Turkey/Egypt draft resolution of 1950, adding preamble paragraphs and listing provisions the covenant should include (participation in government, self-determination, employment, social security, education and other economic and social rights) and State obligations to implement them.
first.evidence: Text of the amendment covers several distinct rights (political participation, self-determination, work, social security, education) plus implementation duties; A/1559 para. 25 describes its vote as an insertion of three preamble paragraphs. The A/2929 ICCPR tags are mere document lists spread across articles 19, 21, 22.

second.subject: USSR amendments to the Brazil-Turkey-UK joint draft resolution on the draft covenant (GA 5th session, 1950), adding preambular paragraphs and listing provisions to include (political participation, self-determination, work, social security, education and other ESC rights).
second.evidence: Text: 'Amendments to joint draft resolution submitted by Brazil, Turkey and [UK]', adds preamble paragraphs and a list of several rights; A/1559 para. 25 records vote on 'insertion of three additional paragraphs in the preamble (A/C.3/L.96)'. A/2929 cites it under several articles (19, 21, 22). Touches many articles; it is a resolution amendment.

first.subject: Secretariat compilation of the texts of the preambles, article 1 and the substantive articles adopted so far by the Third Committee for both draft Covenants.
first.evidence: Text opens: the Committee has adopted the preambles and article 1 of both covenants, articles 6 to 16 of the ICESCR draft and 6 to 26 of the ICCPR draft, and reproduces them; A/C.3/L.1017 says the adopted articles are reproduced in L.978. Speeches cite it only for article 10 ICESCR as an example, so the ICCPR 24 tags do not fix it to one article.

second.subject: Secretariat compilation of the texts adopted so far by the Third Committee (preambles, article 1, ICESCR arts 6-16, ICCPR arts 6-26).
second.evidence: Text: 'Up to the present, the Third Committee has adopted the preambles and article 1 of both ... The texts, as adopted, are as follows'; A/C.3/L.1017 describes it as reproducing the articles adopted so far. The ICCPR 24 tags come from speeches citing its art. 10 while debating the Polish child article, not its subject.

sonnet.note: Compilation of the articles adopted so far in both draft Covenants, not a proposal on one article.

opus.note: Compilation of the texts adopted so far for both draft Covenants (preambles, art. 1, many articles); the Covenants as a whole.

first.subject: Polish sub-amendment to the United Kingdom amendment (E/CN.4/L.85) on the right to education: non-discrimination, State duty to provide the school system, scholarships, higher education, fundamental education, and the aims of education.

first.subject: Text of the preamble of the draft Covenant as adopted by the Commission on first reading in 1950.
first.evidence: The document reproduces only the preamble, which is not a numbered article. SR.199 has the Rapporteur reading it out. The A/2929 concordance lists it under 'Preamble'. The pipeline's ICCPR 2 tag on the E/1992 citation is just a footnote reference.

first.subject: Lebanon's amendment to the USSR amendment on trade union rights: adds a paragraph in which States undertake to guarantee everyone the free exercise of this right.
first.evidence: SR.298 introduces it with 'article 27' and the USSR amendment L.50/Rev.1, alongside the Yugoslav trade union amendments. SR.300 (France) says it gives the article the same juridical value as the article on the right of association. Draft article 27 of 1952 became ICESCR 8.

second.subject: Lebanon's sub-amendment to the USSR amendment (E/CN.4/L.50) on trade union rights: adds a paragraph by which States guarantee to everyone the free exercise of this right.
second.evidence: In SR.298 the Chair takes it up among the amendments to article 27 (trade union rights). In SR.300 France supports it as giving article 27 the same legal force as the right of association. Draft 27 at CHR 8 maps to ICESCR 8 in the concordance, and the tagged citation is ICESCR 8.

sonnet.note: Lebanon sub-amendment to USSR trade union rights amendment (art 8).

opus.note: Lebanese sub-amendment to the USSR trade union rights amendment (draft art. 27): guarantee free exercise of the right (ICESCR 8).

first.subject: Lebanon's amendment to Yugoslavia's amendment: States Parties undertake to guarantee the free exercise of the right to form and join trade unions of one's choice, local, national and international.

second.subject: Lebanon's sub-amendment to Yugoslavia's amendment (E/CN.4/L.78): States undertake to guarantee everyone's free exercise of the right to form and join local, national and international trade unions of his choice.

sonnet.note: Lebanon sub-amendment to Yugoslav amendment: right to form and join trade unions (art 8).

opus.note: Lebanese sub-amendment to Yugoslav amendment: right to form and join trade unions (ICESCR 8(1)(a)).

first.subject: Belgium's amendment to France's amendment, adding a paragraph: the family, the basis of society, is entitled to the widest possible protection, and is based on marriage entered into with the free consent of the intending spouses.
first.evidence: The text is on protection of the family and free consent to marriage. E/CN.4/669 para. 139 and SR.298 record it as adopted and forming a paragraph of the family, mothers and children article. It amends the French amendment L.74/Rev.1, which is that article. The tagged speech reads ICESCR 10, which matches the text. Marriage consent also appears in ICCPR 23, but the proposal is made in the ICESCR family-protection article.

second.subject: Belgium's amendment to France's amendment: adds a paragraph saying the family, the basis of society, is entitled to the widest possible protection and is based on marriage entered into with the free consent of the intending spouses.
second.evidence: Text on family protection and free consent to marriage. The French amendment it modifies is E/CN.4/L.74, on draft art. 26 (E/CN.4/669 lists L.74/Rev.1 under article 26). Adopted 13-3-2 as paragraph 3 (E/CN.4/669 para. 139, SR.298). Concordance chr8 art. 26 = ICESCR 10.

sonnet.note: Belgium: protection of the family, based on marriage with free consent (art 10(1)).

opus.note: Belgian addition: family as basis of society entitled to widest protection, marriage by free consent (became para. of ICESCR 10(1)).

first.subject: United States amendment (with Rev.2) to France's draft article: nothing in the Covenant may be read as implying a right to destroy the rights, or as limiting or derogating from rights recognized under any State's law or conventions.
first.evidence: The text is a saving clause (no destruction of rights, no derogation from rights under domestic law or other conventions). In SR.303 Mrs Roosevelt says paragraph 1 reproduces the original draft saving article and that her amendments broaden paragraph 2 of the French proposal. The tagged speech reads ICESCR 5, which matches. The Commission was drafting the economic, social and cultural covenant in 1952.

second.subject: US amendment (and Rev.2) to the French draft article E/CN.4/L.67. Nothing in the Covenant implies a right to destroy the rights it recognizes or to limit them more than it permits, and nothing limits or derogates from rights recognized under domestic law or other conventions.
second.evidence: The text is the anti-destruction clause and the savings clause of ICESCR art. 5(1)-(2). E/CN.4/669 p. 44 footnote groups E/CN.4/L.67 and L.114/Rev.1-2 with L.168-174. SR.303 (Roosevelt) says it reproduced original draft article 18 of E/1992. The one tagged citation is ICESCR 5.

sonnet.note: US amendment to French article: nothing in the Covenant to be interpreted as destroying or limiting rights; saving clause (art 5).

opus.note: US amendment to French saving-clause article ('Nothing in this Covenant may be interpreted as...'; no derogation from rights under national law or conventions); 8th session ESC covenant, citing tagged ICESCR 5. Same clause also exists as ICCPR 5.

first.subject: United States amendment to France's amendment (L.76): replace 'public order and' with 'for the prevention of disorder and for the', in the general limitations clause.

SR.306 (French delegation on the limitation formula proposed by the United States, L.115) and SR.308 (Roosevelt: no longer needed once the words were deleted from the French amendment) place it in the limitations debate. Two of the three tagged speeches read ICESCR 4. The SR.297 citation, tagged ICESCR 10, attributes L.115 to Egypt's child-labour amendment, which is L.116, and looks like an OCR or attribution slip.

second.subject: US amendment to France's amendment (E/CN.4/L.76) to the general limitations clause: replace 'public order and' with 'for the prevention of disorder and for the'.
second.evidence: E/CN.4/669 p. 69 lists it as the US amendment to France's amendment to article 32 (E/CN.4/L.76). The p. 44 footnote cites E/CN.4/L.76, 115 and 175 with SR.306-308. Concordance chr8 art. 32 = ICESCR 4. SR.306 and SR.308 (tagged ICESCR 4) discuss it. The ICESCR 10 tag in SR.297 is a slip for the Egyptian L.116.

sonnet.note: US amendment to French limitations clause (replace 'public order and'); the debate on it is in the limitations discussion (SR.306). The SR.297 mention is a mis-citation for Egypt's L.116.

opus.note: Document text: US sub-amendment to French limitations clause replacing 'public order and' (SR.306 discussion of general-welfare limitations, ICESCR 4). One SR.297 citation attributing L.115 to Egypt on child labour appears to be a misprint for L.116.

first.subject: Egypt's amendment to the revised French amendment: replace paragraph 3 so that young persons are not required to do work likely to hamper their normal development, and illegal use of child labour is made a penal offence.

second.subject: Egypt's amendment to France's revised amendment (E/CN.4/L.74/Rev.1): young persons not to be required to do work harmful to their development, and illegal child labour to be a penal offence.

sonnet.note: Egypt: child labour and protection of young persons from exploitation (art 10(3)).

opus.note: Egyptian amendment to French text: protection of young persons, child labour exploitation a penal offence (ICESCR 10(3)).

first.subject: USSR amendments to draft article 10: equality before courts, independent judges, and a free interpreter and right to address the court in one's own language for accused persons.

first.subject: USSR amendment replacing draft article 14 with a freedom of opinion, speech and press guarantee limited by a ban on war propaganda, hatred incitement and slander.

first.subject: USSR amendment adding to draft article 17 a legal prohibition of propaganda for fascist or nazi views or for racial and national exclusiveness, hatred and contempt.
first.evidence: The text proposes a prohibition of propaganda of hatred, which is the content of final ICCPR 20. It was attached to draft art. 17 (chr8 concordance: 17 -> 26, equality), so the pipeline tags ICCPR 26, and the report E/CN.4/669 votes on it under that article. Chosen by subject, not by the draft number.

second.subject: USSR addition to draft article 17 (equality and non-discrimination) requiring the law to prohibit propaganda for fascist or nazi views and for racial or national exclusiveness, hatred and contempt.

first.subject: Text of draft article 23 as adopted on first reading: opening for signature or accession, ratification, entry into force after 20 ratifications, and Secretary-General's notifications.
first.evidence: The text combines final-clause matters that became several covenant articles (ICCPR 48 signature and ratification, 49 entry into force). Citing footnotes point to different final articles (ICCPR 48, 51, ICESCR 23, 26) and are inconsistent, so no single article is fixed.

second.subject: Text of draft article 23 as the Commission adopted it at first reading in 1950: signature, ratification and accession, deposit with the Secretary-General, entry into force after 20 instruments, and notification.

second.subject: India amendment to the preamble of the draft covenant, replacing 'Recognizing' with 'Reaffirming' in its third paragraph.

first.subject: Proposes an amendments clause: a State party may propose an amendment, a conference is convened if one-third of States favour it, and amendments take effect once approved by the General Assembly and accepted by two-thirds of the States parties (Schachter, 1950).

second.subject: Proposes the text of the amendment clause (how States Parties propose amendments, a conference, General Assembly approval, and entry into force for the States that accept them).
second.evidence: The text is an amendment procedure clause. E/CN.4/SR.197 (1950) quotes it and the Commission adopted Schachter's text. sonnet.note: Amendment procedure text, drafted for the single Covenant; final ICCPR 51 and ICESCR 29 both correspond, so no single instrument.

opus.note: Amendment procedure for the 1950 single (civil and political) draft covenant, cited in E/1681. Its lineage also runs to ICESCR 29

first.subject: France: amendment to draft article 9 deleting the words "in all cases" (procedure in expulsion of aliens).

SR.316 discusses France's L.153 within the article 9 debate, on whether procedure is laid down by law. Tag ICCPR 13 agrees. SR.318 calls L.153 an amendment to article 10 para 3, but this looks like an OCR or citing slip: the document itself says article 9.

second.subject: France proposes to delete the words 'in all cases' from article 9 (expulsion of aliens) of the 1951 draft.

E/CN.4/SR.316-317 debate it under article 9 on expulsion, tagged ICCPR 13. The SR.318 mention of 'L.153' as a US amendment to article 10 is an OCR or symbol slip.

opus.note: France amendment to draft art. 9 (1952 numbering = expulsion of aliens) deleting 'in all cases'; SR.316-317 discussion of art. 9.

first.subject: France: amendment (Rev.2) to draft article 10 on fair trial: adds "in a democratic society", amends the public-hearing exceptions (private lives of the parties), and provides for compensation for a miscarriage of justice unless the non-disclosure is attributable to the person.
