second.subject: France proposes to amend article 10 on fair trial: add 'in a democratic society' to the grounds for excluding the public, add the private lives of the parties, and add a proviso barring compensation for a miscarriage of justice when the convicted person caused the non-disclosure of the fact.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 10' (public hearing, compensation for miscarriage of justice). The chr8 concordance maps draft art. 10 to ICCPR 14. E/CN.4/669 records the votes on L.154/Rev.2 under the fair trial article, and E/CN.4/SR.323 debates it under article 10.

sonnet.note: France amendment to draft article 10: public hearing, judgments, compensation for miscarriage of justice; final ICCPR 14.

opus.note: French amendment to draft article 10: public hearing limits ('in a democratic society') and compensation for miscarriage of justice. Final ICCPR 14.

first.subject: France: revised amendment to draft article 14, paragraph 3: the exercise of freedom of expression carries special duties, and restrictions are allowed only if provided by law and strictly necessary in a democratic society (rights of others, national security, public order, health, morals).
first.evidence: The document names article 14, which the concordance maps at chr8 to final ICCPR 19. SR.320 (Cassin) says L.156 avoids enumerating limitations on freedom of expression. The tag is ICCPR 19 on all 5 tagged citing passages.

second.subject: France proposes a revised paragraph 3 of article 14 on freedom of expression: special duties and responsibilities, and restrictions only as provided by law and strictly necessary in a democratic society.
second.evidence: Text: 'revised amendment to article 14'. The chr8 concordance maps draft art. 14 to ICCPR 19. Cassin in E/CN.4/SR.320 speaks of limits on freedom of expression. Five citing speeches, all tagged ICCPR 19. E/CN.4/669 records its adoption.

sonnet.note: France revised amendment to para 3 of draft art. 14: limitations on freedom of expression (Rev.1 text).

opus.note: France revised amendment to draft art. 14 para. 3: duties, responsibilities and restrictions on expression.

first.subject: France: amendment to draft article 17 (equality before the law and non-discrimination) deleting the part of the article after the words "of the law".
first.evidence: The document names article 17. The concordance maps chr8 draft art. 17 to final ICCPR 26. The single citing passage (SR.327, Bracco) is about the non-discrimination clause in article 17 and is tagged ICCPR 26.

second.subject: France proposes to delete the part of article 17 (equality before the law) that follows the words 'of the law', which is the non-discrimination clause.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 17'. The chr8 concordance maps draft art. 17 of E/1992 to ICCPR 26. In E/CN.4/SR.327 (tagged ICCPR 26), Uruguay argues to keep the non-discrimination clause in article 17.

sonnet.note: France amendment to draft art. 17 (equality before the law, non-discrimination), delete after 'of the law'.

opus.note: France amendment to draft art. 17 deleting text after 'of the law' (non-discrimination clause) -> equality before the law.

first.subject: France: amendment to draft article 4 replacing "against his will" with "without his consent" (medical or scientific experimentation without free consent).
first.evidence: The document names article 4. The concordance maps chr8 draft art. 4 to final ICCPR 7. E/CN.4/669 para. 177 reports the vote on L.159 ("without his free consent") under article 4, and A/2929 lists it in the documentation for article 7.

second.subject: France proposes to replace 'against his will' with 'without his consent' in article 4, on medical or scientific experimentation.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to article 4' (8th session, 1952). The chr8 concordance maps draft art. 4 to ICCPR 7. E/CN.4/669 para. 177 records its adoption as 'without his free consent' in the torture and experimentation article. A/2929 lists it under that article, tagged ICCPR 7.

sonnet.note: France amendment to draft art. 4: 'against his will' to 'without his consent' (medical or scientific experimentation, torture article); ICCPR 7.

opus.note: France amendment to draft art. 4: 'against his will' -> 'without his consent' (medical experimentation) -> torture/ill-treatment.

first.subject: French amendments to draft article 1 of the civil and political covenant: delete 'within its territory and', and recast paragraph 3(a)-(c) on ensuring remedies.
first.evidence: Text amends article 1 paras 1 and 3 (undertaking, remedies). Concordance chr8 ICCPR draft 1 -> final 2. E/CN.4/669 paras 271, 275 and SR.328 (Juvigny) discuss 'within its territory' and judicial remedy. The SR.310 tag ICCPR 6 is wrong (a passing Egypt mention).

second.subject: France amends draft article 1 of the civil and political covenant: delete 'within its territory and' from paragraph 1 and reword paragraph 3 on remedies.
second.evidence: The text is headed 'amendment to article 1' and deals with 'within its territory and' (para 1) and remedies (para 3), both of which ended up in ICCPR 2(1) and 2(3). E/CN.4/669 paras 271 and 275 record the votes on it under that article, and in SR.328 Juvigny introduces it. The SR.310 citation tagged ICCPR 6 looks like an OCR or citation error.

sonnet.note: France amendment: delete 'within its territory and'; para 3 on judicial remedy. Obligations of States and remedies, ICCPR 2 (draft art. 1 numbering differs).

opus.note: France: deletes 'within its territory and' and amends the remedies paragraph (3(a)-(c)) of the general obligations article; the report cites it under ICCPR 2.

first.subject: Chile's amendment to the USSR revised trade union amendment (L.50/Rev.1): non-discrimination clause in para 1 and new paras 3-4 on trade union autonomy and non-dissolution.
first.evidence: Text is about trade union constitutions, non-interference and dissolution. E/CN.4/669 para 141 and SR.300 (all tagged ICESCR 8). Concordance chr8 ICESCR draft 27 -> final 8, meeting 300.

second.subject: Chile amends the USSR's revised trade-union amendment (E/CN.4/L.50/Rev.1): adds non-discrimination to the right to form and join trade unions, and adds paragraphs on unions' freedom to set their own rules and protection from administrative dissolution.
second.evidence: The text is entirely about the right to form and join trade unions and about trade-union autonomy. E/CN.4/669 para 141 and SR.300 treat it under the trade-union article, and the citing tags are ICESCR 8 (2 of 2).

sonnet.note: Chile amendment on trade union organizations' constitutions, non-dissolution by administrative authority: trade union rights.

opus.note: Chile: amends the USSR trade union article (E/CN.4/L.50/Rev.1). Its content covers the right to form and join trade unions without discrimination, trade union constitutions and dissolution.

first.subject: Chile and Yugoslavia's proposed preamble for the draft covenant on economic, social and cultural rights (dignity, freedom from fear and want, Charter obligations).
first.evidence: Text is preamble recitals. E/CN.4/669 para 161 and SR.308 call it a proposal for a preamble; A/2929 cites it under preamble discussion. A preamble is not an article, so none.

second.subject: Chile and Yugoslavia propose a preamble for the draft covenant on economic, social and cultural rights.
second.evidence: The text is preamble wording ('Considering...', 'Recognizing...', 'agree upon the following articles'). E/CN.4/669 para 161 calls it 'a proposal for a preamble to the draft covenant on economic, social and cultural rights', and A/2929 cites it under the preamble. The catalogue has no ICESCR preamble entry.

first.subject: Polish amendment to the US revised amendment to France's draft article: nothing in the Covenant may limit or derogate from a higher standard of economic, social and cultural rights already attained in a State.
first.evidence: Text replaces paragraph 2 of the saving clause. SR.304 (tagged ICESCR 5) and SR.305/306 treat it as a variant of the French saving-clause proposal (L.67/Rev.1), which is the article that became ICESCR 5.

second.subject: Poland amends the US amendment to France's draft saving-clause article: in paragraph 2, nothing in the Covenant may limit or derogate from a higher standard of economic, social and cultural rights already reached in a State.
second.evidence: The text replaces paragraph 2 of the French draft article (E/CN.4/L.67/Rev.1). That article is the ESC covenant's counterpart of the civil covenant's article 18 saving clause, and it became ICESCR 5(2). SR.304-306 discuss it with the other L.67 amendments, and the one tagged citation is ICESCR 5.

sonnet.note: Poland amendment to para 2 of France's draft: nothing to limit or derogate from higher standard attained. Saving clause.

opus.note: Poland: amends paragraph 2 of the French draft article so that the Covenant cannot derogate from a higher standard of economic, social and cultural rights. This is the saving clause, ICESCR 5(2).

first.subject: Chilean amendment to France's draft article: no restriction of or derogation from economic, social and cultural rights recognized in any country on the pretext that the Covenant does not recognize them or does so to a lesser extent.
first.evidence: Text replaces paragraph 2 of the French saving-clause article. E/CN.4/669 para 154 and SR.305 (four tags ICESCR 5) discuss it as an amendment to paragraph 2 modelled on article 18 of the other draft.

second.subject: Chile amends paragraph 2 of France's draft article: no restriction on or derogation from economic, social and cultural rights recognized or existing in a country, on the pretext that the Covenant does not recognize them or recognizes them less.
second.evidence: The wording is almost that of the final ICESCR 5(2). E/CN.4/669 para 154 records the vote on paragraph 2, and all 4 tagged citations (SR.305, E/CN.4/669) are ICESCR 5.

sonnet.note: Chile amendment to para 2 of France's draft: no restriction upon or derogation from existing rights. Saving clause.

opus.note: Chile: replaces paragraph 2 of the French draft article (no restriction on rights existing under national law or conventions). This is the saving clause, ICESCR 5(2).

first.subject: UK amendment to France's draft article: nothing in the Covenant may be interpreted as abridging or permitting derogation from any recognition or guarantee of human rights under a State's law or other conventions.
first.evidence: Text amends paragraph 2 of the French saving-clause article. SR.305 (tagged ICESCR 5), SR.306 and E/CN.4/669 treat it alongside L.67/Rev.1, L.168 and L.169, the article that became ICESCR 5.

second.subject: The United Kingdom amends paragraph 2 of France's draft article: nothing in the Covenant may abridge or permit derogation from human rights recognized under a State's law or conventions.
second.evidence: The text is a saving clause amending paragraph 2 of the French draft article E/CN.4/L.67/Rev.1, which became ICESCR 5(2). SR.305 and 306 debate it alongside L.169 and L.168, and the citing tags are ICESCR 5 (2 of 2).

sonnet.note: UK amendment to para 2 of France's draft: nothing in Covenant abridging or permitting derogation from existing guarantees. Saving clause, debated with L.168/169 at SR.305.

opus.note: UK: amends paragraph 2 of the French draft article (no abridging of rights guaranteed by national law or conventions). Same saving clause, debated at SR.305, so ICESCR 5(2).

first.subject: Australia and Sweden propose adding to the preamble of the draft covenant on economic, social and cultural rights a paragraph on the individual's duties to other individuals and to his community and his responsibility to strive for the promotion and observance of the rights.
first.evidence: Text is an amendment to the preamble proposed by the USA/Chile-Yugoslavia; E/CN.4/669 para. 161 and SR.308 say it was voted with the Chile-Yugoslav preamble (L.167) and accepted by the sponsors. It concerns the preamble, which has no article number; the concordance lists the ICESCR preamble as a separate item (meetings 308, 333).

second.subject: Australia and Sweden propose to add to the preamble of the draft ESC covenant a paragraph on the individual's duties to others and to the community and his responsibility to promote the rights in the Covenant.
second.evidence: The text inserts a paragraph after the fourth paragraph of the preamble; E/CN.4/669 para. 161 and SR.308 confirm that it amended the Chile-Yugoslavia preamble (E/CN.4/L.167). It concerns the ICESCR preamble, which has no article number and is not in the catalogue.

first.subject: Polish amendment to the French proposal (L.67/Rev.1) for a saving clause, adding that recognition of rights in national laws or conventions applies only if they are not contradictory to the Covenant and the Charter.
first.evidence: The stored text is a duplicate of L.171 (Australia-Sweden preamble amendment, same document number 52-5031), so it is a mis-scan; the debates decide. SR.305 and SR.306 name L.172, L.173 and L.174 as Polish amendments to the Chilean, French (L.67/Rev.1) and UK proposals; France's L.67 is the new article that became ICESCR 5 (concordance chr8, meetings 303-306); sister document L.174 confirms the wording. The SR.309 citation (genocide, tagged ICCPR 6) is probably a mistyped symbol for another L number.

second.subject: Poland proposes to amend the French draft saving clause (E/CN.4/L.67/Rev.1) for the ESC covenant so that it applies only where the national laws and conventions do not contradict the Covenant and the Charter.
second.evidence: The variant text in the file is a copy of E/CN.4/L.171 (the Australia-Sweden preamble paragraph), so it is not this document's text. SR.305 (Boratynski) says the Polish amendments L.172, L.173 and L.174 were to the Chilean, French and UK proposals respectively. SR.306 (Azkoul) says L.173 amended the French draft article L.67/Rev.1, which Kovalenko says reproduced ICCPR draft art. 18 (now ICCPR 5, the saving clause). That makes it ICESCR art. 5(2). The SR.309 passage tagged ICCPR 6 (genocide in article 3) is most likely an OCR misreading of another symbol.

sonnet.note: Australia and Sweden amendment inserting a paragraph in the preamble of the draft economic, social and cultural covenant: preamble, not an article.

opus.note: Australia and Sweden: inserts a paragraph on the individual's duties into the preamble of the economic, social and cultural covenant. The preamble is not in the catalogue. The citing passages refer to other documents numbered L.173.

first.subject: Poland proposes an amendment to the UK amendment to the French saving-clause article, adding that laws and conventions are respected only if not contradictory to the provisions and spirit of the Covenant and the UN Charter.
first.evidence: Own text is an amendment to the UK amendment (L.170) to the French article (L.67/Rev.1); SR.305 (tagged ICESCR 5) and SR.306 discuss it; the concordance maps France's L.67 (meetings 303-306) to final ICESCR 5.

second.subject: Poland proposes to add to the UK amendment (E/CN.4/L.170) of the French saving clause the condition that the laws and conventions do not contradict the Covenant and the UN Charter.
second.evidence: The text is an amendment to the UK amendment L.170 of the French draft article, adding 'if these laws and conventions are not contradictory to... the present Covenant and the Charter'. SR.305 (Boratynski, Hoare) and SR.306 (Azkoul, Kovalenko) place it in the debate on the saving clause modelled on ICCPR draft art. 18, which is now ICESCR art. 5(2). Two speeches are tagged ICESCR 5.

sonnet.note: Polish amendment to the saving clause (UK, French and Chilean texts); the debate is tagged ICESCR 5 in both citing passages, so the instrument is less certain.

opus.note: Polish sub-amendment to the UK text of the French saving-clause article (rights recognised by law or conventions a State is party to); discussed in 1952 for the ESC covenant, now ICESCR art. 5(2).

first.subject: Chile proposes, as an amendment to the French amendment to the general limitation article, a paragraph saying that certain rights (self-determination, work, social security, protection of mothers and children, adequate standard of living, health, education, culture, equality of men and women) cannot be subject to any limitation.
first.evidence: SR.308 (tagged ICESCR 4) ties it to article 32 of the E/1992 draft as amended by France; concordance chr8 maps draft ICESCR article 32 (meetings 306-308) to final article 4 (limitations).

second.subject: Chile proposes to add to the French amendment (E/CN.4/L.76) of the general limitations article a paragraph listing the ESC rights (self-determination, work, social security, food, health, education, and so on) that can never be limited.
second.evidence: The text concerns rights that 'cannot be subject to any limitation'. SR.308 places it in the vote on article 32 as amended by France. The CHR concordance at chr8 (E/1992) maps ICESCR draft art. 32 to final art. 4 (the limitations clause), debated at meetings 306-308. Two speeches are tagged ICESCR 4.

sonnet.note: Chile amendment to France's amendment on the limitation article: lists rights that cannot be limited. Amends the limitations clause (ICESCR 4).

opus.note: Chile: amends the French amendment to the general limitations article (draft art. 32), listing rights that cannot be limited. This is the limitations clause, ICESCR 4.

first.subject: Australian amendment to paragraph 2(b) of the draft article on freedom of movement, replacing 'a national' with 'a citizen or national and in which he has his permanent home', later reworded to 'his own country' (the right to return).
first.evidence: E/CN.4/669 (tagged ICCPR 12) describes Australia's L.189/Rev.1 as changing the expression to 'his own country', adopted 10-2-6; SR.316 puts L.189/Rev.2 to the vote on paragraph 2(b); concordance chr8 maps draft article 8 (meetings 315-316) to final ICCPR 12.

second.subject: Australia proposes to change 'a national' in paragraph 2(b) of the article on freedom of movement to cover a citizen or national, or a person whose permanent home is there, on the right to return to one's own country.
second.evidence: The text amends paragraph 2(b) on the country of which a person is 'a national'. E/CN.4/669 says the Australian amendment (L.189/Rev.1) brought in 'his own country' for the right to return, adopted 10-2-6. SR.316 records the vote on paragraph 2(b). Both citing passages are tagged ICCPR 12 (art. 12(4)).

sonnet.note: Australia amendment to para 2(b): right to return to 'his own country' (national/citizen). Freedom of movement.

opus.note: Australia: changes paragraph 2(b) from 'a national' to 'his own country' (right to return). This is ICCPR 12(4).

first.subject: Compilation of the economic, social and cultural rights articles adopted by the Commission in May 1951 (7th session): work, just conditions of work, social security (L.19); adequate standard of living, health (Add.1); maternity and children (Add.2); trade unions (Add.3); education (Add.4); limitations and progressive realization (Add.6); reporting (Add.7).
first.evidence: The variants Add.1-Add.7 each carry different articles; the document as a whole covers ICESCR 6, 7, 9, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 4, 2 and 16-17 equally. The citing passages (E/1992 footnotes) cite it separately for housing (11) and education (13), so no single article fits.

second.subject: The texts of the ESC articles the Commission adopted in April-May 1951: work, conditions of work, social security, standard of living, health, mothers and children, trade unions, education, limitations, general undertaking and reporting.
second.evidence: The base document and its addenda (Add.1-Add.7) are compilations of many adopted articles: ICESCR 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 10, 8, 13, 4, 2 and 16-17. E/1992 cites it in footnotes for several different articles. No single article dominates.

first.subject: French amendment to the Chile-Uruguay-Yugoslavia and USSR proposals for a new article 9a: everyone has the right to seek asylum from persecution, States to strive to ensure its effective granting, not invocable for non-political crimes or acts contrary to UN purposes.
first.evidence: The text proposes the new article 9a on asylum, which it amends; it was debated at SR.317-318 (1952) alongside draft article 9 (expulsion of aliens, final ICCPR 13), hence the pipeline's ICCPR 13 tag. No asylum article was adopted in the ICCPR, so no final article.

second.subject: French sub-amendment redrafting the proposed new article 9a on the right to seek asylum from persecution (amending the Chile/Uruguay/Yugoslavia and USSR amendments).
second.evidence: Text: 'Amend the proposed text of article 9a to read: Everyone has the right to seek asylum from persecution...'. SR.317-318 (1952) debate on asylum; the asylum article was never adopted in the ICCPR. Pipeline tag ICCPR 13 (expulsion of aliens) reflects the meeting's article, not this proposal's subject.

first.subject: US sub-amendment to the French amendment (L.156/Rev.1) on freedom of expression: replace 'liabilities, restrictions and penalties' with 'limitations'.
first.evidence: E/CN.4/669 cites it as an amendment to the French amendment L.156/Rev.1 in the debate on freedom of information and expression; concordance covenant_drafts_chr.csv: 1952 draft article 14 = final ICCPR 19; meetings 320-322 (SR.320 June 3, 1952).

second.subject: US sub-amendment to the French amendment (E/CN.4/L.156/Rev.1) replacing 'liabilities, restrictions and penalties' with 'limitations' in the freedom of expression article.
second.evidence: E/CN.4/669 report: US amendment L.192 to French amendment L.156/Rev.1 on the freedom of information clause, rejected 7-6-5; same vote sequence as the UK amendment on freedom of expression (ICCPR 19).

sonnet.note: US amendment to France's amendment L.156/Rev.1 on restrictions and penalties in the freedom of expression article; voted at SR.320, tagged ICCPR 19.

opus.note: US: amends the French amendment (L.156/Rev.1) on freedom of expression, replacing 'liabilities, restrictions and penalties' with 'limitations'. This is ICCPR 19.

first.subject: US amendment to the UK amendment on freedom of expression: replace 'the medium of any lawfully operated devices' with 'any other media' in paragraph 1 and 'formalities, conditions, restrictions or penalties' with 'limitations' in paragraph 2.
first.evidence: Text concerns media and restrictions on expression; E/CN.4/669 and SR.320 (3 June 1952) cite it in the freedom of expression debate; concordance: 1952 draft article 14 = ICCPR 19.

second.subject: US amendment to the UK amendment on freedom of expression: 'any other media' for 'the medium of any lawfully operated devices', and 'limitations' for 'formalities, conditions, restrictions or penalties'.
second.evidence: Text itself (media of expression, restrictions); E/CN.4/669 records its rejection in the vote on the freedom of information article; citing speech tagged ICCPR 19.

sonnet.note: US amendment to UK amendment: 'any other media', and 'limitations' replacing formalities and restrictions. Opinion and expression.

opus.note: US: amends the UK amendment on freedom of expression ('any other media'; 'limitations'). This is ICCPR 19.

first.subject: USSR draft resolution reaffirming that a single covenant on all human rights should be prepared, rather than two covenants, and asking ECOSOC to refer the revision of GA resolution 543 (VI) to the Assembly.
first.evidence: The text is a draft resolution on the single versus two-covenant question; SR.333 (12 June 1952) debates it as such with the Australia-France-India proposal L.210. It concerns the Covenants as a whole.

second.subject: USSR draft resolution reaffirming the need for a single covenant and asking ECOSOC to refer revision of GA resolution 543 (VI) to the General Assembly.
second.evidence: Text is a draft resolution on one vs two covenants; SR.333 and E/CN.4/669 para. 96 discuss it as such; no article tags.

first.subject: US amendment to the Yugoslav amendment to draft article 17: second sentence to read 'All persons shall be accorded equal protection of the law.'
first.evidence: Text names article 17 of the 1952 draft (E/1992 annex III); concordance covenant_drafts_chr.csv: draft article 17 = final ICCPR 26 (meetings 326-328); SR.327 speech tagged ICCPR 26 cites it.

second.subject: US amendment to the Yugoslav amendment to draft article 17, making the second sentence read 'All persons shall be accorded equal protection of the law.'
second.evidence: Text on equal protection of the law (the equality/non-discrimination clause, final ICCPR 26); SR.327 (1952) speech tagged ICCPR 26 discussing an autonomous equality clause applying beyond Covenant rights.

sonnet.note: US amendment to Yugoslav amendment on equal protection of the law (draft art. 17); cited under ICCPR 26.

opus.note: US amendment to Yugoslav amendment to draft art 17: 'All persons shall be accorded equal protection of the law'; equality before the law

first.subject: Lebanese amendment to the third paragraph of the preamble of the draft covenant on civil and political rights: insert 'are inalienable and' before 'flow from the inherent dignity of the human person'.
first.evidence: The text amends the preamble, not an article; the only citing passage (A/2929 para. 6) discusses the preamble's foundation of rights in human dignity. No final article corresponds.

second.subject: Lebanese amendment to the third paragraph of the preamble of the draft covenant on civil and political rights, inserting that the rights are 'inalienable'.
second.evidence: Text: 'amendment to the preamble ... third paragraph'; the preamble is not a numbered article, so no final article applies.

first.subject: USSR draft resolution to insert in the covenants an article on the right of peoples and nations to self-determination (with a third paragraph on national minorities' language and schools, which was rejected).
first.evidence: Text opens with the self-determination article; E/CN.4/669 paras 58-68 and SR.256-261 show it as the base text for the 1952 debate that produced the common Article 1 of both Covenants (the minorities paragraph was voted down 9-4). Article 1 is identical in ICCPR and ICESCR; the tagged debates say ICESCR 1 or ICCPR+ICESCR 1.

second.subject: USSR draft resolution to insert in the covenants an article on the right of peoples and nations to self-determination, with a third paragraph (rejected) on national minorities' language and schools.
second.evidence: The text proposes an article on the right of every people and nation to self-determination. E/CN.4/669 paras. 58 and 68 treat it as the basis of the article adopted at the 256th-261st meetings, which became common Article 1 (ICCPR 1 = ICESCR 1). The citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 1 (6/6). The minorities paragraph was rejected 9-4, so it does not point to Article 27.

sonnet.note: USSR draft resolution inserting an article on the right of peoples and nations to self-determination. It also has a minorities sentence, but the debate treats it as the self-determination proposal.

opus.note: USSR draft resolution to insert an article on the right of peoples and nations to self-determination in the covenants. It also has a paragraph on minority languages and schools, but its subject is self-determination.

first.subject: Yugoslav draft resolution proposing an article on the right of peoples to self-determination, including the right of each person to take part in action for the people's independence (Rev.1 shortened it to that clause).
first.evidence: Text of L.22 and L.22/Rev.1 is about self-determination; E/CN.4/669 paras 65 and 72 and SR.260 discuss it as an addition to the self-determination article; Rev.1 was rejected 6-6-6, but the subject is common Article 1 (identical in ICCPR and ICESCR).

second.subject: Yugoslav draft resolution to include a self-determination article (right of peoples, including secession, and of every person to take part in it); Rev.1 reduced it to the individual's right to take part in the independence of their people.
second.evidence: The text reads 'Decides to include the following article ... All peoples have the right to self-determination'. E/CN.4/669 paras. 65 and 72 record it as a proposal on the self-determination article (Rev.1 rejected 6-6-6). SR.260 (Yugoslavia) ties it to the article adopted. The article is common Article 1 of both Covenants (ICESCR 1 is equally correct), and A/2929 lists it in the documentation on that article.

first.subject: UK amendments to a series of articles (35, 36, 38, 40, 41, 42 and others) in Part IV of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, on election, terms and vacancies of the Human Rights Committee.
first.evidence: The text lists amendments to several separate articles of Part IV (measures of implementation); the citing passages (A/2929 documentation, E/CN.4/689) cite it under draft Articles 35-42 with tags ICCPR 32, 34, 36, 41. It does not concentrate on one article, so no single final article.

second.subject: United Kingdom amendments to draft articles 35-42 and following of Part IV (measures of implementation) on election, re-election, vacancies and terms of office of Human Rights Committee members.
second.evidence: The text amends articles 35, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41 and 42 of E/2256 Part IV. In the final ICCPR these are spread over arts. 29-34 and more. A/2929 and E/CN.4/689 cite it under several articles (tags ICCPR 32, 34, 36, 41), so no single article fits.

first.subject: Egyptian revised amendments to the USSR draft (L.21): all peoples to have the right to self-determination, namely freely to determine their political, economic, social and cultural status, and all States bound to assist in ensuring it.
first.evidence: Text of L.23/Rev.1 is about self-determination; E/CN.4/669 paras 58-72 record the Polish sub-amendment and votes on its words 'All peoples and all nations shall have the right to self-determination', which became Article 1 (identical in both Covenants).

second.subject: Egyptian revised amendments to the USSR self-determination article (E/CN.4/L.21): 'All peoples shall have the right to self-determination, namely the right freely to determine their political, economic, social and cultural status', and a duty of all States to help ensure it.
second.evidence: The text amends E/CN.4/L.21. E/CN.4/669 (votes: 'All peoples and all nations shall have the right to self-determination' adopted 12-0-6) shows it shaped the adopted text, which became common Article 1 para. 1 of both Covenants (ICESCR 1 is equally correct). Citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 1 (3/3).

sonnet.note: Egypt's amendments to the USSR self-determination text (all peoples' right freely to determine their status; States bound to assist).

opus.note: Egypt's revised amendments to the USSR self-determination draft (L.21): 'All peoples shall have the right to self-determination...'.

first.subject: USSR proposal to include in both draft Covenants an article that the Covenant's provisions extend to all parts of federal States without limitation or exception.
first.evidence: Text of L.230 and E/CN.4/689 (section B, proposals for a federal State article, 'text proposed for inclusion in both draft covenants') show it is the federal-State clause; final ICESCR 28 (ICCPR 50 in the other Covenant); the citing passage is tagged ICESCR 28.

second.subject: USSR proposal to include in both covenants an article extending their provisions to all parts of federal States without limitations or exceptions.
second.evidence: The text 'The provisions of the Covenant shall extend to all parts of federal States without any limitations or exceptions' is almost word for word the adopted federal clause, ICCPR art. 50 = ICESCR art. 28. E/CN.4/689 annex lists it as the proposal for a federal State article, and one citing passage is tagged ICESCR 28.

first.subject: French draft resolution on the Commission's procedure for examining measures of implementation (Part IV of the civil and political draft, Part V of the economic draft, in a stated order).
first.evidence: Text is a procedural resolution about order of work on implementation; SR.346 (1953-04-14) introduces and adopts it as a procedure for the exchange of views, not an article proposal.

second.subject: French draft resolution on the Commission's procedure for examining measures of implementation (the order in which Parts IV and V of the two drafts are taken up).
second.evidence: The text is a procedural resolution ('Decides to examine: 1. Part IV ... 2. Part V ...'). E/CN.4/SR.346 records it as a draft resolution on procedure, adopted part by part. It is about no article.

first.subject: Chile's draft resolution to add to the self-determination provision of both Covenants that the right of peoples includes permanent sovereignty over natural wealth and resources and that no people may be deprived of its means of subsistence.
first.evidence: Text: 'The right of the peoples to self-determination shall also include permanent sovereignty over their natural wealth and resources... in no case may a people be deprived of its own means of subsistence'. E/CN.4/669 para 67 says it was for both covenants; debated with the USSR, Yugoslav and Indian self-determination proposals (paras 58, 67); all 5 tagged speeches are ICESCR 1. The wording is that of common article 1(2) (article 1 is the same in both Covenants, ICCPR 1 = ICESCR 1); not the later ICCPR 47 / ICESCR 25 saving clause.

second.subject: Chilean draft resolution to include in both Covenants a provision that the right of peoples to self-determination includes permanent sovereignty over their natural wealth and resources and that no people may be deprived of its own means of subsistence.
second.evidence: Text: 'The right of the peoples to self-determination shall also include permanent sovereignty over their natural wealth and resources... in no case may a people be deprived of its own means of subsistence'; E/CN.4/669 paras 58, 67 list it among the proposals for the self-determination article (256th-261st meetings); all 5 tagged citing speeches ICESCR 1. The idea became paragraph 2 of common article 1 (ICCPR 1 and ICESCR 1 alike).

sonnet.note: Chile: right of self-determination to include permanent sovereignty over natural wealth and resources, for both covenants.

opus.note: Chilean proposal: self-determination includes permanent sovereignty over natural wealth and resources; no people deprived of its means of subsistence (now art. 1(2)).

first.subject: Belgian substitute text for draft article 52 (inter-State complaints to the Committee, with the Committee acting as conciliating organ, plus petitions from individuals received for information).
first.evidence: Header: 'Amendment to Part IV, Article 52 (E/2256, Annex I, Section D)'. covenant_drafts_chr.csv maps chr9 draft 52 to final ICCPR 41. E/CN.4/689 para 127: 'a substitute text for the whole of the article'. All 10 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 41; SR.355-356 list it under 'Article 52 and ... amendments thereto'.

second.subject: Belgian substitute text for article 52 of the measures of implementation: inter-state communications to the Committee, which is to seek a settlement and act as a conciliating organ, plus petitions from individuals received for information.
second.evidence: Heading: 'Amendment to Part IV, Article 52 (E/2256, Annex I, Section D)'; E/CN.4/689 para 127 says it proposed a substitute text for the whole article; covenant_drafts_chr.csv maps chr9 draft art 52 to ICCPR 41; citing speeches tagged ICCPR 41 (10). Its petition part fell outside the Covenant (later the Optional Protocol).

sonnet.note: Belgian amendment substituting the text of draft Art. 52 (State-to-State communications, conciliation by the Committee), which became ICCPR 41. Its paragraph 2 on individual petitions has no final counterpart in the Covenant.

opus.note: Belgian substitute text for article 52 of the 1953 implementation draft: State-to-State communications to the Committee and conciliation. Para. 2 on petitions from individuals has no final ICCPR article (Optional Protocol matter).

first.subject: Chilean amendments to draft article 52: 'and urgent' cases in paragraph 3, and new paragraphs on Committee action, communications from NGOs and individuals, and admissibility rules.
first.evidence: Header: 'Amendments to Article 52 of Part IV, Annex I, Section D, Measures of Implementation'. Concordance chr9 draft 52 = final ICCPR 41. E/CN.4/689 para 130 records the adoption of the 'and urgent' amendment to paragraph 3; all 11 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 41.

second.subject: Chilean amendments to article 52 of the measures of implementation: 'and urgent' cases in paragraph 3, plus new paragraphs letting the Committee act on its own initiative and receive communications from NGOs and from individuals backed by them.
second.evidence: Heading: 'Amendments to Article 52 of Part IV, Annex I, Section D (E/2256)'; E/CN.4/689 paras 130-131 (paragraph 3 amendment adopted, additional paragraphs); concordance chr9 draft art 52 maps to ICCPR 41; citing speeches tagged ICCPR 41 (11).

sonnet.note: Chile's amendments to draft Art. 52 (para. 3 'urgent cases', new paras on NGO communications); Art. 52 became ICCPR 41, and the para. 3 amendment was adopted.

opus.note: Chile's amendments to article 52 (1953): 'and urgent' cases in para. 3 (exhaustion of remedies, now art. 41(1)(c)), plus new paragraphs on communications from NGOs and individuals (not retained in the Covenant).

first.subject: Indian draft resolution (and Rev.1) for an article on the right of peoples to self-determination, to be included in the Covenants, with States' undertaking to promote or guarantee its free exercise.
first.evidence: Text: 'All peoples have a right to self-determination' / Rev.1: 'All people shall have the right of self-determination... States parties... shall undertake to promote or guarantee the free exercise of that right'. E/CN.4/669 paras 58 and 66 (debate on the self-determination article, 256th-261st meetings); the 3 tagged speeches are ICESCR 1. Common article 1 (ICCPR 1 = ICESCR 1).

second.subject: Indian draft resolution to include in the Covenants an article on the right of all peoples to self-determination, with States parties (including administering powers) to promote or guarantee its exercise.
second.evidence: Text (Rev.1): 'Resolves that the following article be included in the draft International Covenants: All people shall have the right of self-determination...'; E/CN.4/669 paras 58, 66; citing speeches tagged ICESCR 1 (3). This was the article that became common article 1 (ICCPR 1 and ICESCR 1 alike).

sonnet.note: India's draft article on the right of peoples to self-determination (and Rev.1).

opus.note: India's draft article on the right of all peoples to self-determination, for inclusion in the covenants (with Rev.1).

first.subject: Joint Chilean-Indian amendment to draft article 52: Committee's own initiative in serious cases, and receipt of communications from NGOs and from individuals or groups supported by an NGO, with admissibility rules.
first.evidence: Text: paragraphs 4-6 on Committee competence to receive communications, maintaining Chile's amendment L.246 to paragraph 3. SR.358 and SR.360 describe it as a combined amendment to article 52; concordance chr9 draft 52 = final ICCPR 41; all 3 tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 41.

second.subject: Joint Chilean-Indian amendment adding paragraphs to article 52 of the measures of implementation: the Committee acting on its own initiative, and receiving communications from NGOs in consultative status and from individuals backed by them.
second.evidence: SR.358 says Chile and India combined their amendments to article 52 into E/CN.4/L.252; E/CN.4/689 para 131; SR.360 agenda 'Article 52 and ... joint Chilean-Indian amendments'; concordance chr9 draft art 52 maps to ICCPR 41; tags ICCPR 41 (3).

sonnet.note: Chile/India joint amendment adding paragraphs on Committee initiative and communications to the draft implementation article (draft art. 52) that became the communications article; moderately confident.

opus.note: Chile-India joint amendment adding paragraphs to draft art. 52 (the committee's handling of complaints, i.e. inter-State communications): committee initiative and NGO/individual communications. The individual-petition substance ended up in the Optional Protocol

first.subject: Uruguayan amendment to paragraph 5(b) of the joint Chilean-Indian amendment to draft article 52: individuals who are injured parties may petition directly or through an NGO.
first.evidence: Text: 'Amendment to the revised amendments of Chile and India (E/CN.4/L.252/Rev.1) to Article 52 of Part IV, Annex I, Section D'. Voted on in SR.362 with the article 52 amendments; concordance chr9 draft 52 = final ICCPR 41; both tagged citing speeches are ICCPR 41.

second.subject: Uruguayan amendment to paragraph 5(b) of the joint Chilean-Indian amendment to article 52, letting individuals who are victims petition the Committee directly or through an NGO.
second.evidence: Heading: 'Amendment to the revised amendments of Chile and India (E/CN.4/L.252/Rev.1) to Article 52 of Part IV, Annex I, Section D (E/2256)'; SR.362 votes on it; concordance chr9 draft art 52 maps to ICCPR 41; tags ICCPR 41 (2).

sonnet.note: Uruguay's amendment to the Chile-India revised amendment on draft Art. 52 (para. 5(b), who may communicate); Art. 52 became ICCPR 41. The subject is individual petitions, which is not in the final Art. 41, so this is less certain.

opus.note: Uruguay's amendment to para. 5(b) of the Chile-India amendment to article 52 (1953, the communications article, now art. 41). Its subject is petitions from individuals, which ended up in the Optional Protocol and not in art. 41. Treat as a borderline answer.

first.subject: Chile proposes inserting the words "hatred and" before "violence" in the Sub-Commission's proposed additional article on condemning incitement to violence against religious, national, racial or minority groups.
first.evidence: Text amends the Sub-Commission's additional article on incitement (E/2256, Annex II, Section A). E/CN.4/689 para. 37 and SR.379 debate it as an amendment to that proposal, and the citing speeches are tagged ICCPR 20. That article became ICCPR 20 (advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred).

second.subject: Chile's amendment to the Sub-Commission's proposed additional article condemning incitement to violence against religious, national or racial groups; it inserts 'hatred and' before 'violence'.
second.evidence: The text itself says it amends the Sub-Commission's additional article on incitement (E/2256, Annex II, A). E/CN.4/689 para. 37 and E/CN.4/SR.379 discuss it with the Polish amendment L.269, and A/2929 cites it under the incitement article. That article became ICCPR 20 (advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred).

sonnet.note: Chile's amendment to the Sub-Commission proposal on incitement to hatred and violence; cited in the ICCPR 20 (incitement to hatred) discussion.

opus.note: Chile's amendment to the Sub-Commission's article condemning incitement to violence against religious, national or racial groups: inserts 'hatred and'.

first.subject: USSR draft resolution asking ECOSOC to propose that the General Assembly review resolution 543 (VI) so that the two covenants are merged back into a single one.
first.evidence: The text calls the division into two covenants artificial. E/CN.4/689 paras. 32 and 40 and SR.390 treat it as a resolution on the structure of the covenants. It concerns no single article. The later text in this file is an E/CN.4/L.331 fragment appended by mistake.

second.subject: USSR draft resolution asking ECOSOC to have the General Assembly review resolution 543 (VI), which split the draft covenant into two covenants.
second.evidence: The text is a draft resolution calling the division into two covenants artificial. E/CN.4/SR.390 lists it as the 'Soviet Union draft resolution on the division of the draft covenant'. It is about the Covenants as a whole, not any one article. The OCR variant also carries unrelated L.331 text.

first.subject: Texts adopted by the Commission in March 1954 on periodic reports under the draft economic, social and cultural covenant, provisionally numbered Articles 60-67 and 69 (Add.1 covers 67 and 69).
first.evidence: The document spans several draft articles. E/CN.4/705 footnotes cite it for draft Articles 64-66 and 69, and E/CN.4/L.272 notes it as Articles 60-67 and 69. In the final ICESCR they correspond to several articles (16-18, 19, 22, 23 and 24), so no single article fits.

second.subject: Texts the Commission adopted on 5 and 8 March 1954 for the ICESCR system of periodic reports (draft arts. 60-67 and 69).
second.evidence: The text sets out draft articles 60, 61, 62, 63 and, in Add.1, 67 and 69. E/CN.4/705 cites it for draft arts. 64, 65, 66 and 69. These drafts correspond to several final ICESCR articles (16-24), so no single article applies.

first.subject: France proposes a new article letting States Parties to the economic, social and cultural covenant accept, right by right and subject to reciprocity, the Human Rights Committee's inter-State complaints procedure for that covenant.
first.evidence: The text is a draft article for the ICESCR referring to articles 27 et seq. of the civil and political covenant. SR.431 titles it 'Applicability of the Human Rights Committee procedure to the Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights'. No such provision exists in the final ICESCR, so it became no article.

second.subject: French proposed draft article letting States Parties to the economic, social and cultural covenant accept, right by right, inter-State complaints under the Human Rights Committee procedure.
second.evidence: E/CN.4/705 para. 216 calls it a 'draft article' proposed by France. In E/CN.4/SR.431 it is taken under 'Applicability of the Human Rights Committee procedure to the Covenant on economic, social and cultural rights'. No such article is in the adopted ICESCR.

first.subject: United Kingdom draft reservations article (with Add.1 on withdrawing reservations as soon as practicable), covering circulation and acceptance of reservations by two-thirds of States.
first.evidence: E/CN.4/705 paras. 265-268 present it as a draft article on reservations, with amendments from the USSR and France. The Commission did not adopt any reservations article, and neither covenant has one. The single A/2929 tag (ICESCR 24) does not fit the text.

second.subject: United Kingdom draft reservations article for the covenant; Add.1 adds a paragraph on withdrawing reservations.
second.evidence: The text is headed 'Draft Reservation Article'. E/CN.4/705 paras. 265-268 say the Commission sent it to the General Assembly without deciding, together with the amendments. Neither adopted Covenant has a reservations article. A/2929's single tag (ICESCR 24) comes from a footnote list and is not reliable.

first.subject: USSR amendment to the United Kingdom's draft reservations article (L.345): permit reservations to any provision at signature or acceptance, and delete the circulation and two-thirds acceptance rules.
first.evidence: The text expressly amends the UK draft reservations article E/CN.4/L.345. E/CN.4/705 paras. 265 and 268 confirm this. No reservations article became part of either covenant.

second.subject: USSR amendment to the United Kingdom's draft reservations article (L.345): allow reservations to any provision and delete the acceptance procedure.
second.evidence: The text says it amends the UK draft reservations article E/CN.4/L.345. E/CN.4/705 paras. 265 and 268 say the same. The reservations article was never adopted, so there is no final article.

first.subject: China, Egypt, Lebanon and the Philippines propose a new article on reservations to the Covenant (compatibility test, objections, ICJ referral, withdrawal).
first.evidence: The text is a draft article on reservations. The Commission's 1954 report (E/CN.4/705) lists it among the competing reservation proposals sent to the General Assembly. No reservations article appears in the adopted ICCPR or ICESCR.

second.subject: China, Egypt, Lebanon and the Philippines propose a new article on reservations to the Covenant: reservations compatible with its object and purpose, objections, referral of disputes to the ICJ, and withdrawal.
second.evidence: The text is headed 'draft article on reservations'. E/CN.4/705 paras 265ff list it among the reservations proposals that the Commission (10th session, 1954) sent on to the General Assembly without adopting. Neither adopted Covenant has a reservations article, so no final article.

first.subject: France proposes to amend paragraph 4 of the United Kingdom draft reservations article, replacing 'three months' with 'one year' for objecting to a reservation.
first.evidence: The text amends the UK draft reservations article (L.345). E/CN.4/705 para. 282 discusses the one-year period. The reservations article was not adopted, so there is no final article.

second.subject: France amends the United Kingdom's draft reservations article (E/CN.4/L.345), changing the period for objecting to reservations from three months to one year.
second.evidence: The text reads 'amendment to the draft reservations article submitted by the United Kingdom'. E/CN.4/705 paras 269 and 282 describe it the same way. It amends a proposed new reservations article that never entered either Covenant, so no final article.

first.subject: The USSR proposes amendments to the four-power draft reservations article (L.351): reservations to any provision, no objections or ICJ dispute procedure, withdrawal only of reservations.
first.evidence: The text says it amends the draft reservations article in L.351. SR.447 (Morozov) and E/CN.4/705 para. 272 confirm this. No reservations article was adopted.

second.subject: The USSR amends the four-power draft reservations article (E/CN.4/L.351): reservations to any provision allowed, the Covenant in force between reserving and other States except for the reserved provisions, and the ICJ and objection paragraphs deleted.
second.evidence: The text reads 'amendment to the draft reservations article proposed in document E/CN.4/L.351'. See E/CN.4/705 para 272 and Morozov in E/CN.4/SR.447. The proposed reservations article was never adopted, so no final article.

first.subject: Chile and Uruguay propose a draft article that would prohibit any State Party from making reservations to the Covenant's provisions.
first.evidence: The text reads 'No State Party to this Covenant may make reservations in respect of its provisions.' E/CN.4/705 lists it as the Chile-Uruguay draft article on reservations. It was not adopted, and the final Covenants contain no reservations article.

second.subject: Chile and Uruguay propose a new article providing that no State Party may make reservations to the Covenant.
second.evidence: The text reads 'No State Party to this Covenant may make reservations in respect of its provisions'. E/CN.4/705 lists it as proposal (c) among the reservations drafts sent to the General Assembly. There is no reservations article in either final Covenant.

first.subject: Belgium proposes a sub-amendment to Pakistan's procedural amendment (L.356) to the Chile-Uruguay reservations proposal, so that Belgium's proposal (L.348) is also transmitted to the General Assembly as a pertinent document.
first.evidence: The text adds 'and the proposal of Belgium (L.348)' to the Pakistan amendment. SR.449 shows the sub-amendment concerns which documents are treated as pertinent, which is a matter of procedure and not the substance of an article.

second.subject: Belgium sub-amends Pakistan's amendment (E/CN.4/L.356) to the draft resolution on transmitting the reservations documents to the General Assembly, adding Belgium's own proposal (E/CN.4/L.348) to the list of documents sent.
second.evidence: The text only adds the words 'and the proposal of Belgium (E/CN.4/L.348)'. In E/CN.4/SR.449 the Belgian delegate says the purpose is that Belgium's proposal be treated as a pertinent document. It is a procedural motion about which documents to transmit.

first.subject: Compilation of the final clauses adopted at the Commission's 10th session: draft articles 70 (signature, ratification, entry into force), 71 (federal States), 72 (territories) and 73 (amendments).
first.evidence: The text sets out draft articles 70-73 as adopted at the 450th and 451st meetings. E/CN.4/L.272 maps articles 70 and 71 to later articles 26/51 and 27/52. The document covers several distinct articles equally, so no single final article applies.

second.subject: Texts of the final-clause articles 70-73 as adopted at the Commission's 450th and 451st meetings (1954): signature, ratification and entry into force; federal States; territorial application; amendments.
second.evidence: The document gives draft articles 70 (signature and ratification), 71 (federal clause), 72 (territorial clause, from GA resolution 422 (V)) and 73 (amendments). E/CN.4/L.272 says these became articles 26-29 of the economic, social and cultural covenant and 51-54 of the civil and political covenant. The final equivalents include ICESCR 26, 28 and 29 and ICCPR 48, 50 and 51. The document therefore spans several articles of both Covenants, and no one of them dominates.

first.subject: Rapporteur's suggested arrangement and numbering of the provisions of the two draft Covenants for the report of the tenth session (1954).
first.evidence: Text is an order-of-work and arrangement note listing article ranges and sources for every part of both Covenants; E/CN.4/705 cites it as the basis on which the Commission decided the order and numbering of the articles. Not about any single article.

second.subject: Rapporteur/Secretariat suggestion on the arrangement, order and numbering of all provisions of both draft Covenants for the tenth-session report.
second.evidence: Text sets out Parts I-V and article ranges of both draft Covenants; E/CN.4/705 says the order and numbering were decided on the basis of these suggestions (E/CN.4/L.378). Concerns the Covenants as a whole.

first.subject: USSR amendments to draft article 21 on just and favourable conditions of work: delete 'minimum' in the remuneration sub-paragraph, equal pay for women, and rest and leisure in the working-hours sub-paragraph.
first.evidence: Text amends draft article 21 (work conditions: remuneration, equal work, reasonable hours). E/CN.4/669 paras 112-115 report the votes on L.46 paras 1 and 3 under article 21, which became ICESCR 7; citing speeches are tagged ICESCR 7 (8 of 9).

second.subject: USSR amendments to draft article 21 (just and favourable conditions of work): delete 'minimum' in remuneration, equal pay and conditions for women, rest/leisure and State guarantee of holidays.
second.evidence: Text 'Draft amendments to Article 21' on remuneration, equal pay for equal work, reasonable hours; E/CN.4/669 paras 112-115 record votes on it under article 21 'just and favourable conditions of work'; 8 of 9 tagged citations ICESCR 7.

sonnet.note: USSR amendments to draft Art. 21: fair wages, equal pay for women, conditions of work; this became ICESCR 7.

opus.note: USSR amendments to article 21 (1952) on conditions of work: equal pay, women's working conditions, and rest guaranteed by law or collective agreement.

first.subject: USSR amendment to draft article 22 adding the right to social insurance, the cost to be borne by the State or the employer.
first.evidence: Text amends article 22 on social security; E/CN.4/SR.284 and E/CN.4/669 para 118 discuss it as an amendment on social insurance/social security (draft art. 22 = ICESCR 9); tagged ICESCR 9.

second.subject: USSR amendment to draft article 22 adding the right to social insurance and that the cost of social security be borne by the State or employer.
second.evidence: Text 'Amendment to Article 22' on 'the right of everyone ... to social security'; E/CN.4/669 para 118 and E/CN.4/SR.284 discuss it as the social security article; tag ICESCR 9.

sonnet.note: USSR amendment on social insurance and social security.

opus.note: USSR amendment to draft art. 22: social insurance and social security

first.subject: USSR amendment to draft article 23 adding an undertaking to ensure by legislation a dwelling consistent with human dignity.
first.evidence: Text amends article 23 (standard of living, housing); E/CN.4/669 para 130 reports it rejected 11-6 under article 23 (food, clothing, housing), which became ICESCR 11; A/2929 documentation list places it under article 11; tagged ICESCR 11.

second.subject: USSR amendment to draft article 23 obliging States to adopt measures, particularly legislation, to ensure everyone a dwelling consistent with human dignity.
second.evidence: Text 'Draft amendment to Article 23'; E/CN.4/669 para 130: rejected USSR amendment on dwellings in the article on housing (China's 'food, clothing and' housing); A/2929 documentation maps it to final article 11; tags ICESCR 11.

sonnet.note: USSR amendment to draft Art. 23 on a dwelling consistent with human dignity; this became ICESCR 11 (housing).

opus.note: USSR amendment to article 23 (1952): measures to ensure everyone a dwelling consistent with human dignity (housing, standard of living).

first.subject: Texts of draft articles 16 (freedom of thought, conscience and religion) and 17 (freedom of opinion and expression) as adopted by the Commission on first reading, 1950.
first.evidence: Document itself sets out two articles equally; they correspond to ICCPR 18 and 19, and the citing documentation (E/1681, A/2929) cites it under both ICCPR 18 and ICCPR 19, so it does not concern a single article.

second.subject: Texts of draft articles 16 (freedom of thought, conscience and religion) and 17 (freedom of opinion and expression) as adopted by the Commission in first reading.
second.evidence: Text reproduces both articles 16 and 17, corresponding to final ICCPR 18 and 19; E/1681 and A/2929 cite it in documentation of both articles. Touches two articles equally.

first.subject: USSR amendment (with Rev.1) to draft article 27 on trade union rights: right to form and join trade unions, protection against interference, right to strike, international affiliation.
first.evidence: Text is wholly about trade-union rights under draft article 27; E/CN.4/669 para 141 and the A/2929 documentation list place L.50/Rev.1 under article 27 = ICESCR 8; citing speeches tagged ICESCR 8 (6 of 6).

second.subject: USSR amendment (and Rev.1 redraft) to draft article 27 on trade union rights: non-discrimination, protection from interference, right to strike, international federations.
second.evidence: Text 'amendment to Article 27' entirely on trade union rights and the right to strike; E/CN.4/669 para 141 and A/2929 documentation list it under final article 8; tags ICESCR 8 (6).

sonnet.note: USSR amendment to draft Art. 27 on trade union rights, the right to strike and international union affiliation; this became ICESCR 8.

opus.note: USSR amendment and Rev.1 to article 27 (1952) on trade union rights, including the right to form and join unions and the right to strike.

first.subject: USSR amendment to the draft education article: the State must guarantee free compulsory primary education by providing a school system, and progressively free higher education by scholarships and a system of higher educational institutions.
first.evidence: Text: amendment to article 23 (sub-paragraphs 3 and 5 on primary and higher education). SR.285 (Morozov) says it strengthens the education article by making the State ensure the right to education. Commission report E/CN.4/669 lists it under the education article (draft art. 28 of 7th session), which became ICESCR 13; tags are ICESCR 13 x6.

second.subject: USSR amendment to the education article adding that the State shall guarantee the right by a school system (primary education) and by scholarships and higher educational institutions.
second.evidence: Text: primary education compulsory and free, higher education progressively free; Corr.1 names article 28 of the seventh-session draft (E/1992), which the concordance maps to ICESCR 13; Morozov introduces it at E/CN.4/SR.285 on the right to education; all 6 tagged citing speeches ICESCR 13.

sonnet.note: USSR amendment on compulsory free primary education and progressively free higher education (draft art. 23 or 28 in the OCR); final art. 13.

opus.note: USSR amendment to the education article (draft art. 28): free compulsory primary education guaranteed by a school system; scholarships for higher education.

first.subject: USSR amendment to draft article 30 (science and culture): add an undertaking to ensure the development of science and education in the interests of progress, democracy and peace.
first.evidence: Text: draft amendment to Article 30, paragraph 1, after 'science and culture'. E/CN.4/669 footnote for the article on conservation, development and diffusion of science and culture (final ICESCR 15) lists L.52; SR.292 Morozov introduces it; tags ICESCR 15 x5.

second.subject: USSR amendment to article 30 (science and culture) adding an undertaking to ensure the development of science and education in the interests of progress, democracy, peace and co-operation among peoples.

second.subject: Australia proposes, in paragraph 8 of draft article 28 (education), to replace 'minimum standards laid down by the State' with 'minimum educational standards approved by the State'.
second.evidence: The text names article 28, paragraph 8, and the parents' choice of schools meeting minimum educational standards, which became ICESCR 13(3). Whitlam introduced it in SR.285, and the SR.287 debate on article 28 was all tagged ICESCR 13.

opus.note: Australian amendment to draft art. 28 para. 8: schools meeting minimum educational standards (parental choice of school)

first.subject: France proposes a sub-amendment to Chile's amendment (E/CN.4/L.53) to draft article 20, replacing it with the words 'and the need for a full employment policy', to be added at the end of the article.
first.evidence: The text says 'amendment to the amendment submitted by Chile ... article 20'. The 1952 draft article 20 is the right to work (ICESCR 6). SR.276 to SR.278 discuss the French sub-amendment in the debate on article 20 and full employment, and the tags are ICESCR 6 (3 speeches). The single ICESCR 13 tag is out of line with the rest.

second.subject: France proposes a sub-amendment replacing Chile's amendment (L.53) to article 20 (right to work) with the words 'and the need for a full employment policy' at the end of the article.
second.evidence: The text refers to 'the end of the present text of article 20' and to full employment. In SR.276-278 (tagged ICESCR 6) it is debated as an amendment to Chile's L.53 on the article on the right to work.

sonnet.note: France amendment adding a full employment policy to the right-to-work article.

opus.note: France sub-amendment to Chile's amendment to draft art. 20 adding 'need for a full employment policy' (right to work)

first.subject: Chile proposes a new article after draft article 21, requiring States Parties to adopt legislative and other measures to give concrete effect to the rights in draft articles 20 and 21 (work, just conditions of work), especially steady economic expansion and full productive employment.
first.evidence: The text is headed 'new article to be inserted after article 21'. It covers two articles, the right to work and the conditions of work, equally. E/CN.4/669 para. 116 records the vote on it as an additional article, which was rejected. It did not become a final article. The joint text L.93 was the one adopted, as a paragraph of the work article.

second.subject: Chile proposes a new article after article 21 requiring States to adopt legislative and other measures to implement the rights in articles 20 and 21 (work and conditions of work), in particular full employment.
second.evidence: The text says 'new article to be inserted after article 21'. E/CN.4/669 para. 116 records that the proposal for an additional article was rejected on a roll-call vote, 10 to 5 with 3 abstentions, so it did not become a final article.

sonnet.note: Chile proposal for a new article on implementing measures for the work-related rights and full employment; spans general obligation and work articles, unclear single final article.

opus.note: Chilean proposal for a new article after draft article 21, requiring measures to implement draft articles 20 and 21 (work and working conditions), including full employment. It covers two articles equally. The full-employment wording resembles ICESCR 6(2), but the proposal was a separate article, so it is left as none.

first.subject: Lebanon proposes a sub-amendment to the United States amendment (L.82) to Chile's amendment (L.53) to draft article 20: the second paragraph would say the measures taken by each State Party to ensure full exercise of 'this right' shall include (measures such as full employment).
first.evidence: The text is an amendment to the US amendment to Chile's L.53. The Chilean L.53 is the amendment to article 20, the right to work, which became ICESCR 6. SR.277 shows Mrs Roosevelt accepting the Lebanese amendment (E/CN.4/L.92) in the debate on the full employment amendments to article 20. No citing speech carries a tag.

second.subject: Lebanon proposes to amend the second paragraph of the US sub-amendment (L.82) to Chile's amendment (L.53) to article 20, so that it speaks of 'the measures taken by each of the States Parties ... to ensure the full exercise of this right'.
second.evidence: It is a sub-amendment in the L.53/L.82 chain on article 20 (right to work). In SR.277 Roosevelt accepted it with 'the steps to be taken', and that wording became the steps paragraph of ICESCR 6(2).

opus.note: Lebanese amendment to the US amendment (L.82) to Chile's amendment on draft art. 20 (right to work)

first.subject: Lebanon and the United States jointly propose to number the existing text of article 20 as paragraph 1 and to replace Chile's amendment with a paragraph 2. It says the steps to realize the right to work shall include programmes, policies and techniques for steady economic development and full and productive employment under conditions safeguarding fundamental freedoms.
first.evidence: The text names 'Chile ... amendment to article 20' and revises it. E/CN.4/669 records paragraph 2 of the joint amendment (with 'expansion' changed to 'development') adopted as an additional paragraph to the article, which is ICESCR 6(2). SR.278 discusses it in the article 20 debate, and the tags are ICESCR 6. The OCR of the variant also contains unrelated text about article 21 (L.94) and Belgium's article 28, which is scan bleed.

second.subject: Lebanon and the US jointly propose a paragraph 2 for article 20: the steps a State takes to achieve full realization of the right to work shall include programmes, policies and techniques for steady economic development and full and productive employment.
second.evidence: The text names article 20 and gives the paragraph that became ICESCR 6(2). E/CN.4/669 records that paragraph 2 was adopted as an additional paragraph, 9 to 3, and the SR.278 citations are tagged ICESCR 6. The OCR text also contains L.94 and a Belgian amendment that follow it; this answer is based on L.93's own part.

opus.note: Joint Lebanon-US amendment to Chile's amendment to draft art. 20 (right to work, full employment); the OCR text also runs into E/CN.4/L.94 on art. 21

first.subject: Suggestions from the representative of the Commission on the Status of Women, gathering amendments to draft article 21 (Lebanon, Chile, Yugoslavia) on paragraph (b): fair wages and equal pay for equal work for men and women workers.
first.evidence: The heading is 'Article 21 Suggestions made by the representative of the Commission on the Status of Women'. The draft article 21 is just and favourable conditions of work, which became ICESCR 7. SR.280 (tagged ICESCR 7) discusses the 'for men and women workers' wording. E/CN.4/669 para. 104 says the suggestions on the article on conditions of work were circulated as L.94.

second.subject: The Commission on the Status of Women suggests wording for paragraph (b) of article 21 (conditions of work) on fair wages and equal pay for equal work for men and women workers, applied to the Lebanese, Chilean and Yugoslav amendments and to the original text.
second.evidence: The text is headed 'Article 21' and concerns remuneration, fair wages and equal pay, which became ICESCR 7(a). E/CN.4/669 para. 104 says the CSW suggestions on this article were circulated as E/CN.4/L.94, and the citing speech in SR.280 is tagged ICESCR 7.

sonnet.note: Commission on the Status of Women suggestions on fair wages and equal pay for equal work (article on just and favourable conditions of work).

opus.note: CSW suggestions on fair wages and equal pay for men and women workers (just and favourable conditions of work)

first.subject: Belgian amendment to draft article 28 (right to education): progressively free secondary and higher education, aims of education, parental choice of schools and religious/philosophical convictions.
first.evidence: Text says 'amendment to article 28' on paragraphs 4-9 on education; concordance chr8 maps draft 28 to ICESCR 13; all 4 tagged citing speeches (SR.286-288) are ICESCR 13.

second.subject: Belgium's amendment to paragraphs 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 of draft article 28 on education: secondary and higher education made progressively free, the aims of education, and parents' liberty to choose schools and religious education.
second.evidence: Text heads 'Belgium: amendment to article 28' and deals with the right to education; the concordance maps chr8 draft article 28 (E/1992) to ICESCR 13; all 4 tagged citing speeches (E/CN.4/SR.286-289) are tagged ICESCR 13.

opus.note: Belgian amendment to draft art. 28 on education: secondary and higher education, aims of education, parents' liberty

first.subject: Lebanese amendment to the UK amendment (L.85) on draft article 28: right to education, its aims, free primary and progressively free secondary and higher education, parents' liberty to choose schools.
first.evidence: Text is a full education article; E/CN.4/669 paras 120-122 vote on it as amendment to article 28; concordance chr8 28 to ICESCR 13; all tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 13.

second.subject: Lebanon's amendment (and Rev.1) to the United Kingdom amendment (E/CN.4/L.85) to article 28, redrafting the article on the right to education: aims of education, free and compulsory primary education, secondary, higher and fundamental education, and parents' liberty of choice of schools.
second.evidence: Text is a complete redraft of the right to education; E/CN.4/669 paras 120-122 record the vote on L.96/Rev.1 as an amendment to the UK amendment to article 28; draft article 28 (chr8) maps to ICESCR 13; all 6 tagged citations are ICESCR 13.

opus.note: Lebanese amendment (and Rev.1) to the UK amendment to draft art. 28: right to education, its aims, and the steps to realise it

first.subject: Egyptian amendment to the Lebanese amendment (L.96): parents' right to ensure the religious education of their children in conformity with their own convictions.
first.evidence: Amends para III(b) of L.96 on education; cited in SR.287 heading under article 28 (education); concordance maps draft 28 to ICESCR 13.

second.subject: Egypt's sub-amendment to the Lebanese amendment (E/CN.4/L.96) on article 28: parents' right to ensure the 'religious' education of their children in conformity with their own convictions (deleting 'religious and philosophical').
second.evidence: Text amends paragraph III(b) of L.96 on parental choice of schools and religious education, which became ICESCR 13(3); SR.287 lists it among the documents for article 28 (chr8 draft 28 = ICESCR 13).

opus.note: Egypt's sub-amendment to Lebanon's amendment (E/CN.4/L.96), para. III(b): parents' freedom to choose schools other than public ones and to ensure their children's religious education in line with their convictions. This matches ICESCR art. 13(3) (education). The citing record SR.287 is also tagged ICESCR 13 (draft art. 28). The items file was not at the scratchpad path given; the file with the same name one directory up was used.

first.subject: Polish amendment to the US amendment (L.80/Rev.2) to the education article: education shall encourage suppression of incitement to racial and other hatred.
first.evidence: OCR 'article 20' is a misreading of 28 (L.80/Rev.2 is the US amendment to article 28 education, SR.287); SR.288 Polish speaker lists L.98 with L.99 and L.100 as amendments to the Lebanese, UK and US education amendments; all 3 tagged citing speeches are ICESCR 13.

second.subject: Poland's sub-amendment to the revised United States amendment (E/CN.4/L.80/Rev.2) to the article on education, adding that education shall encourage the suppression of all incitement to racial and other hatred.
second.evidence: Text's 'article 20' is OCR for 28: SR.288 says Poland proposed L.98 as an amendment to the US amendment to restore article 28, the education article (chr8 draft 28 = ICESCR 13); the 3 tagged citations are ICESCR 13.

sonnet.note: Polish sub-amendment to the US education amendment (SR.288 debate on education); adds suppression of racial hatred to the education aims.

opus.note: Polish sub-amendment to US amendment on education aims (debated as draft art. 28, education; the 'article 20' in the OCR is a misread)

first.subject: Polish amendment to the Lebanese amendment (L.96): non-discrimination in education, compulsory free primary and progressively free secondary and higher education with State duty to provide schools, aims of education.
first.evidence: Text amends L.96 on education; E/CN.4/669 paras 120-121 report votes on it under article 28; concordance chr8 28 to ICESCR 13. The ICCPR 50-tagged passage cites a different L.99 (Australia, India, US on federal States) from another session, not this document.

second.subject: Poland's sub-amendment to the Lebanese amendment (E/CN.4/L.96) on education: non-discrimination in education, free and compulsory primary education, progressively free secondary and higher education, fundamental education, and the aims of education.
second.evidence: Text amends paragraphs I-III of L.96 on the right to education; E/CN.4/669 paras 120-121 record the votes on it under article 28 (chr8 draft 28 = ICESCR 13). One citation tagged ICCPR 50 quotes a federal clause by Australia, India and the US and is a mis-cited symbol, not this document.

sonnet.note: Poland amendment to Lebanese amendment on education (compulsory free primary, secondary, higher, aims of education); final ICESCR 13.

opus.note: Polish sub-amendment to the Lebanese education amendment (E/CN.4/L.96) on non-discrimination, primary, secondary, higher and fundamental education, and the aims of education. Final ICESCR 13.
